The growing complexity of spatial tasks has increasingly driven the demand for coordination among interdependent tasks and the cooperative participation of mobile workers, which remains relatively unexplored among existing studies. To fill this gap, this paper introduces Dependency-Cooperative Spatial Crowdsourcing (DCSC), a novel problem that explicitly models task dependencies and enables systematic worker cooperation to address complex spatial scenarios. To solve DCSC, we propose a two-stage solution: Dependency-aware Recommendation and Cooperation-aware Matching. In the first stage, we develop a multi-agent reinforcement learning approach enhanced with meta-gradient techniques to recommend suitable subtasks while considering dependency constraints. In the second stage, we propose a genetic algorithm-enhanced game approach to achieve optimal cooperative assignment, guided by a multi-dimensional matching utility function. To ensure consistency and optimization across both stages, we employ meta-gradients from the policy network to guide the optimization of the utility function. Additionally, we utilize graph neural network-based policy clustering to address task heterogeneity, enabling each cluster to learn specialized parameters and enhance reinforcement learning performance. However, existing methods typically rely on the subgraphs produced by a rationale extractor without explicitly assessing their reliability, particularly during early training stages when the extractor is prone to generating inaccurate or biased rationales. Learning with such unreliable rationales can mislead the classifier and further deteriorate rationale quality, ultimately undermining generalization performance. Specifically, CoRas employs a dual-classifier framework to cooperatively select reliable rationales. Motivated by the small-loss criterion, CoRas prioritizes rationales with low prediction loss, while simultaneously selecting rationales with high prediction divergence to mitigate selection bias caused by relying solely on self-predictions during training. This allows CoRas to effectively select reliable rationales for downstream tasks, subsequently enhancing graph rationale learning. are increasingly exposed to diverse cyber-physical attacks that originate in the cyber layer and disrupt physical operation. A critical defense challenge is to rapidly determine whether an attack has occurred and identify its type. To address this challenge, this paper aims to develop a generalized detection scheme capable of identifying multiple types of attacks, particularly unknown ones. It is first observed that, under normal operation, cyber-layer data and physical-layer states are consistent across layers and evolve smoothly over time, while attacks disrupt these consistencies. Building on this insight, a self-supervised Cross-Layer Cross-Temporal Contrastive Learning (CL-CTCL) framework is proposed, which employs a Graph Attention Network-Gated Recurrent Unit (GAT-GRU) encoder to capture spatial dependencies and temporal dynamics. Two complementary contrastive objectives are introduced: Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization (VICReg) for cross-layer alignment and Information Noise-Contrastive Estimation with Momentum Contrast (InfoNCE-MoCo) for temporal consistency. Residual deviations from these consistencies provide reliable attack fingerprints, enabling detection and classification of both known and unknown attacks. However, the “opaque” nature of DL models hinders grid operators from understanding the decision-making processes of these models, affecting model trustworthiness and robustness in diversified diagnosis applications. This paper proposes a hybrid attention-augmented self-interpretable channel-grouped graph convolutional network (HASIG) for diverse short-circuit fault diagnosis of distribution networks, including binary fault detection, faulted line identification, and fault type classification. A channel-grouped graph convolutional network is proposed to learn features from three-phase voltage and current measurements. We present a hybrid attention that combines global edge attention and channel-grouped attention, which can augment the critical features with faithful and robust interpretations during model training, enabling users to gain insights into the predictive behavior inside the model. These three short-circuit fault diagnosis tasks are collaboratively trained under a multi-task learning architecture with interpretable loss constraints. We focus on situational awareness tasks where predictions inherently depend on network-wide spatial relationships through electrical connectivity. Despite extensive research, most ML-based approaches remain system-specific, limiting real-world deployment. This limitation stems from a dual barrier. First, topology changes shift feature distributions and alter input dimensions due to power flow physics. Second, reconfigurations redefine output semantics and dimensionality, requiring models to handle configuration-specific outputs while maintaining transferable feature extraction. Our core insight is treating topology as a learnable dimension through training on diverse reconfigurations, enabling the model to learn universal power flow physics rather than memorizing fixed networks. We achieve this through three synergistic mechanisms: scalar-weight graph convolutions with physics-aware operators handle variable input dimensions and distribution shifts, adaptive pooling maps topology-specific features to unified latent representations, and parallel transformer generates configuration-specific outputs using positional encoding. Our Universal Graph Convolutional Network (UGCN) achieves transferability to any reconfiguration or variation of existing power systems without any prior knowledge of new grid topologies or retraining during implementation. Choices about which entities become nodes, which relationships become edges, and what text each node contains can substantially affect downstream performance. In practice, finding optimal constructions often requires expert knowledge or manual trial and error. We introduce TACO-Graph, a decision tree framework for learning which graph construction choices are most effective for a given dataset and task. Specifically, we focus on text-attributed graphs (TAGs) constructed from multi-attribute tabular data. TACO-Graph enumerates valid TAG representations, scores each using fast proxy evaluation on small representative subsets, and trains an interpretable decision tree on those scores. Across five datasets spanning citation networks, product reviews, and bibliographic relationships, our decision trees predict construction quality on separately drawn evaluation samples with mean Spearman $\\rho$ above $0.9$ for node classification and above $0.8$ for GraphRAG retrieval. Our trees systematically identify which constructions perform better across both GNN and GraphRAG tasks, and the full pipeline is released as an open-source library to support evaluation on new tasks and datasets at https://github.com/AmiriHayes/text_attributed_graphs. propagation characteristics-aware graph neural network with contrastive difficulty guidance for rumor detection","venue":"Journal of Supercomputing","year":2026},{"abstract":"The realm of high-performance computing has expanded to include machine learning tasks of many forms. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are becoming increasingly popular, with their applications expanding across diverse domains. As the scale of graph data continues to grow, including larger numbers of nodes, edges, and higher embedding dimensions, standardized libraries such as DGL and PyG have been developed to facilitate GNN computation. These libraries allow the computation to be described a a high level of abstraction, providing high productivity on the part of the developer. However, with the rapid increase in the number of processor cores and the evolution of multicore architectures, these libraries often show poor scalability and fail to execute GNN inference efficiently on the latest multicore systems, particularly those with upwards of a hundred cores. To address this limitation, we introduce FrontGI, a fast and scalable set of techniques that advances the frontier of GNN inference on large-scale graphs (over 100,000 vertices) by leveraging graph-property- and architecture-aware design. FrontGI employs different parallelization strategies optimized for diverse graph structures, maximizing the utilization of multi-level cache hierarchies in multicore systems. We evaluate a number of GNN models with FrontGI on a 128-core AMD EPYC system. Compared to state-of-the-art libraries, FrontGI achieves up to 3.35$\\times$, 3.20$\\times$, 2.89$\\times$ and 3.10$\\times$ speedups over DGL for GCN, GraphSAGE, GIN, and SGC models, respectively, and even greater improvements over PyG, across a range of large-scale, high-dimensional graph datasets with diverse structural properties.","already_present":false,"authors":["Bing-Lin Ji","Chen-Feng Zhao","R. Chamberlain"],"candidate_id":"candidate-fbe1d3c2c1879fb9844008b9","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.34911","semantic_scholar":"bfba290707eb7ff1d6656ac1103750cd7b65f425"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.34911","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/bfba290707eb7ff1d6656ac1103750cd7b65f425","title":"FrontGI: Architecture-Aware Parallel GNN Inference on Chiplet-Based Multicore Systems","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"A graph neural network (GNN) forecasting a collection of load series combines two mechanisms, sharing parameters across series and reading neighboring series, and a gain over a non-graph model may come from either; telling them apart decides whether a graph is worth maintaining. We propose a model diagnostic protocol that compares the GNN with three reference models: a per-node network, a network shared across nodes without neighbors, and the same GNN without edges. Degree-preserving rewiring tests whether neighbor identity matters. After a tuned benchmark on regional load in France and on low-voltage feeders in the UK, we apply the protocol to deliberately short node histories, as when non-stationary demand leaves only recent observations relevant: the feeders, within one week, and a public dataset of client consumption series. On the feeders, sharing parameters recovers most of the error gap between node-specific models and GNNs, about two thirds against a regularized one. Adding the edges to an otherwise identical backbone brings a smaller gain, half or more of which disappears under rewiring. On the client series, the neighbor mean degrades the per-node model on the shorter window and the edges'gain is not consistently distinguishable from zero; on the regions of France, where each node's own history is already informative, the ranking between per-node models and GNNs changes with tuning. A synthetic study points to noisy local measurements as one regime where neighbors help. In an exploratory online aggregation, graph and non-graph forecasters appear complementary, and the weight assigned to GNNs is not proportional to their contribution. This study proposes a physics-guided framework that integrates a physics-informed Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (PIL-WGAN-GP), a dual-exploration spatiotemporal graph neural network (DEST-GNN), and an arbitrary-quantile recurrent decoder (AQ-RNN). Their empirical coverages were 41.72%, 62.81%, 69.84%, and 85.26%, indicating that structural validity was achieved while calibration remains improvable. Collectively, these findings validate the proposed framework’s ability to bridge physically admissible data reconstruction with reliable, non-crossing probabilistic forecasting for PV clusters.","already_present":false,"authors":["Zhi-Hai Yan","Tian-Yu Xu","Zhong-Kai Shen","Wei Wei","Yu-Hang Huang","Jing-Xuan Long"],"candidate_id":"candidate-5812b67bbf139cddc8054bc8","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.3389/fenrg.2026.1952891","semantic_scholar":"411acacdece47cf233ed0d64d209a1a12949bb0f"},"identity_key":"doi:10.3389/fenrg.2026.1952891","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/411acacdece47cf233ed0d64d209a1a12949bb0f","title":"Physics-guided non-crossing probabilistic forecasting for distributed photovoltaic clusters using dynamic graph attention","venue":"Frontiers in Energy Research","year":2026},{"abstract":"This study focuses on the spatiotemporal prediction of supply chain finance risk contagion and constructs a model based on the dynamic graph attention diffusion mechanism for in-depth exploration. Although existing methods have made substantial progress in intra-domain TF forecasting, inter-domain TF forecasting remains underexplored and faces several fundamental challenges. Specifically, semantic gaps between technologies from different domains hinder effective representation learning; historical inter-domain TFs are highly sparse, limiting the ability to learn reliable structural dependencies; and intra-domain and inter-domain TFs exhibit distinct flow patterns, which are difficult to model within a unified framework. a hybrid deep learning model with feature fusion attention and dual parallel CNN for drug-target binding affinity prediction","venue":"Journal of Supercomputing","year":2026},{"abstract":"Designing optimal auctions for allocating public infrastructure-such as airport slots and energy resources-is challenging due to interdependent resources and complex side-constraints. While the Vickrey-Clarke-Groves (VCG) auction guarantees maximum welfare, it cannot maximize revenue or accommodate the multi-objective trade-offs inherent in public infrastructure systems. We propose a differentiable, constraint-aware framework for combinatorial auction design that enables end-to-end learning of fractionally feasible, approximately strategy-proof mechanisms. Our primary contribution is a combinatorial constraint enforcement technique that ensures fractional feasibility by construction, bypassing the need for penalty-based approximations. We introduce CAGraph, a novel graph-based architecture designed to capture dependencies between items and bidders, alongside CANet and CAFormer as deep learning baselines, for combinatorial settings. We also provide a Matching Pursuit-inspired decomposition that maps fractional allocations to feasible discrete allocations and empirically evaluates the resulting discretization gap. In synthetic benchmarks and an airport slot-divestiture case study, respectively, the learned mechanisms achieve up to 73.5% and 180% higher expected revenue than VCG, under small empirical regret. Finally, we visualize the Pareto frontiers for revenue, welfare, and fairness, providing regulators with a decision-support tool to design infrastructure auctions that balance profitability, efficiency and equity.","already_present":false,"authors":["Mai Pham","Vikrant Vaze","Peter Chin"],"candidate_id":"candidate-c36c345925b43185b2f442af","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.31977","semantic_scholar":"eab9ee1087cb64d6ebec5e47a12bfa0f747940f7"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.31977","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/eab9ee1087cb64d6ebec5e47a12bfa0f747940f7","title":"Differentiable Combinatorial Auction Design: Optimizing Revenue-Welfare-Fairness Frontiers With Graph Attention Networks","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Spatial multi‐omics technologies jointly profile multiple molecular layers in situ, enabling integrated characterization of tissue organization and cellular states. However, many graph-based approaches remain computationally demanding because they rely on repeated message passing over global graphs, whereas naive local sampling may disrupt cell-level correspondence when multimodal features and graph topologies are not induced synchronously. Moreover, simple concatenation or fixed-weight fusion does not explicitly account for unequal uncertainty between expression‐derived and spatial evidence, making the learned representations sensitive to feature corruption, technical noise and modality inconsistency.\n \n \n \n We present SubPoE, a subgraph-induced Product-of-Experts framework for spatial multi‐omics integration. SubPoE synchronously induces aligned local subgraphs from modality‐specific molecular similarity graphs and a shared spatial graph, preserving molecular‐similarity topology correspondence while reducing per‐iteration graph complexity. Dual‐topology variational graph encoders model expression-derived structure and spatial context as probabilistic experts, which are adaptively fused according to their uncertainty through a Product‐of‐Experts formulation. A composite self-supervised objective further improves robustness and cross‐modal alignment.\n \n \n \n Across eight public paired spatial multi‐omics datasets, SubPoE achieves competitive and comparatively stable performance against existing methods. Ablation, sensitivity, robustness and efficiency experiments further support the contributions of synchronous subgraph induction and uncertainty‐aware fusion.\n \n \n \n These results establish SubPoE as an effective approach for learning topology‐preserving, uncertainty-aware representations of heterogeneous spatial multi‐omics data.","already_present":false,"authors":["Yuan-Fang Li","Wen-Tao Gao","Jun-Hao-Ren-Jun-Hao Ren","Qian-Ran Wei","Xin-Lei Wang","Li-Heng Zhang","Rui-Ting Li","Ya-Dong Wang","Xiao Zhang"],"candidate_id":"candidate-2a65d261fc31cbcf6fdea292","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.3389/fgene.2026.1977260","semantic_scholar":"d85b33b5c685ef448d629eb4e1e07e7b4a569331"},"identity_key":"doi:10.3389/fgene.2026.1977260","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/d85b33b5c685ef448d629eb4e1e07e7b4a569331","title":"SubPoE: a subgraph-induced Product-of-Experts framework for spatial multi-omics integration","venue":"Frontiers in Genetics","year":2026},{"abstract":"Manufacturing operators must maintain production while limiting emissions when disturbances spread through shared resources. Learning-based macro placers commonly optimize the macro-only half-perimeter wirelength (HPWL), denoted mHPWL, which ignores standard cell connectivity and spatial demand. In contrast, analytical mixed-size placers optimize differentiable full netlist wirelength and density objectives but are typically unaware of thermal effects. We propose EGGPlacer, an energy-guided diffusion framework that incorporates analytical placement feedback and thermal feedback into macro placement generation. An analytical placer acts as an online physical response model, exposing the standard cell distribution and a full netlist wirelength proxy induced by each intermediate macro placement, while a differentiable thermal model provides temperature feedback. These signals are formulated as composable energies and injected throughout reverse diffusion without retraining the underlying generative model. Experiments on public placement benchmarks show that EGGPlacer achieves competitive mixed-size HPWL relative to strong analytical and learning-based macro placers. In the end-to-end evaluation, EGGPlacer also obtains the lowest average routed wirelength and peak temperature among the evaluated methods. Ablation studies further demonstrate that analytical and thermal guidance provide distinct and complementary benefits across wirelength proxies, routed wirelength, and thermal objectives.","already_present":false,"authors":["Qi Zhou","Guo-Jun Liu","Juan-Hong Zhao","Guang-Zhi Qi","Ze-Hao Chen","Ming Lu"],"candidate_id":"candidate-54364fca714eaf5998590140","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.33099","semantic_scholar":"e8641e4d155b54c7e617c48dd77b7efa73d1d3cf"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.33099","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/e8641e4d155b54c7e617c48dd77b7efa73d1d3cf","title":"EGGPlacer: Energy-Guided Generative Chip Placement with Diffusion Models","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Protein classifiers are highly sensitive to evaluation protocol: random train/test splits induce phylogenetic leakage, allowing models to exploit taxon-specific correlations and substantially overestimate out-of-distribution performance. This issue is particularly acute for venom compound classification by ion-channel target (Ca2+, K+, Na+), where reported accuracies of 80-90% do not reflect generalization to unseen taxa. The persistent-homology representation summarizes backbone geometry through topological descriptors that are robust to local structural perturbations, providing an inductive bias toward phylogenetically invariant learning. Under conventional i.i.d. splits, all models achieve similar accuracy (81-86%), masking differences in inductive bias. Under taxonomic shift, this parity collapses: a sequence-only baseline drops to approximately 30%, the remaining geometric priors cluster at 54-55%, while our persistent-homology model (PH-GNN) achieves 63.4%, outperforming the next-best method by over 8 percentage points. Nevertheless, the current lane detection algorithms may face difficulties in complex driving situations due to poor visual feature extraction, unstable temporal prediction, and inadequate modeling of structural relations between lanes.\n \n \n \n In order to overcome these issues, this paper introduces the unified spatio-temporal graph learning approach that integrates spatial feature extraction, temporal context aggregation, uncertainty-driven graph formation, graph attention reasoning, and geometric optimization. The proposed GraphLane framework dynamically learns graph connections between lane keypoints while incorporating uncertainty estimation to suppress unreliable feature interactions and temporal consistency to improve structural stability across consecutive frames. A geometry-aware optimization strategy is further introduced to encourage smooth and physically consistent lane predictions. The framework was evaluated on the CULane test set using the proposed row-anchor-based lane-existence and localization evaluation.\n \n \n \n Experimental results show that the proposed GraphLane framework achieves a lane-existence precision of 0.9769, recall of 0.8990, F1-score of 0.9363, and an average localization error of 19.28 pixels. Although RAG and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) provide practical ways to enhance LLMs, they remain insufficient for temporal reasoning. Existing retrieval methods typically prioritize semantic relevance while overlooking temporal validity, event order, and evolutionary dependencies, resulting in evidence that is relevant in isolation but temporally fragmented. Meanwhile, conventional PEFT methods usually employ fixed and input-agnostic low-rank updates, making it difficult to capture time-dependent entity semantics and relation drift. To address these limitations, we propose Temporal Evidence-Parameter Co-Alignment (TEPCA), a framework for LLM reasoning over TKGs. TEPCA aligns LLM reasoning with temporal knowledge at both the evidence and parameter levels. At the evidence level, it introduces time-constrained Dynamic Relevance-Guided Path (DRGP) pruning to preserve globally coherent temporal paths, together with Mutual-Information (MI)-based pruning to retain query-informative local facts under temporal constraints. At the parameter level, it integrates Dynamic-Gated LoRA (DG-LoRA), a timestamp-conditioned low-rank adaptation mechanism that dynamically modulates the effective adaptation subspace according to temporal context. However, conveying retrieved graphs through non-unique linear textual contexts to Large Language Models (LLMs) leads to graph-structure degradation and inefficient KV-cache reuse. Meanwhile, graph-structure order optimization is already NP-hard, and the additional KV-cache reuse objective further complicates the search by introducing potentially conflicting orders. To tackle these issues, we propose FuseRAG, a cost-efficient graph-based RAG framework that shifts most retrieved evidence from explicit textual contexts to latent representations. Our main idea is to separate reusable evidence content from query-aware structural interactions in latent space, while retaining only a few explicit facts as semantic anchors. The resulting latent representations are injected into decoder self-attention, where they reshape attention over evidence and thereby influence hidden states and next-token probabilities. However, existing methods face two key challenges when processing sports scenes: on one hand, target distribution in sports footage is strictly constrained by field boundaries, yet generic detectors uniformly allocate detection resources across the entire image, causing frequent false detections in off-field regions due to the visual similarity between spectators and athletes; on the other hand, objects such as athletes, balls, and referees in sports scenes form stable spatial co-occurrence patterns governed by game rules, yet existing methods predict each object independently, failing to leverage cross-category relational cues to assist the detection of difficult targets. To address these issues, this paper proposes SportRGDET (Sport Relation-Graph DEtection Transformer), a framework that achieves accurate detection through two core modules: the Scene Prior Guided Module (SPGM) jointly estimates the spatial probability distribution and boundary gradient map of the field region from multi-scale encoder features, fuses them to generate a hierarchical field confidence mask, and performs spatial modulation on the deformable self-attention weights of the encoder, which reallocates attention resources toward the effective field area and progressively suppresses off-field interference across layers, thereby reducing false detections while incurring only moderate additional computation; the Relation Reasoning Enhancement Module (RREM) treats each candidate object as a node during the detection decoding stage, adaptively learns inter-node association strengths through a relation encoder based on category embeddings and relative spatial positions of node pairs, constructs a dynamic relation graph, and bidirectionally propagates contextual information across nodes via graph attention mechanisms, enabling difficult targets to refine their predictions by leveraging positional and categorical cues from surrounding identified objects, enhancing detection robustness under occlusion and blur conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that SportRGDET achieves significant performance improvements on multiple sports detection benchmark datasets, validating the effectiveness of scene prior and relation reasoning mechanisms in sports scene object detection.","already_present":false,"authors":["Qing-Ya Ouyang","Chao-Yi Su","Qing-Yuan Li"],"candidate_id":"candidate-01b4abd2637fe5dd49f47842","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.1371/journal.pone.0348924","semantic_scholar":"aba7360477948d813a54f2a6d84e6e56fbebafa2"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0348924","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/aba7360477948d813a54f2a6d84e6e56fbebafa2","title":"SportRGDET: Scene prior and relation graph enhanced detection transformer for sports scenes","venue":"PLoS ONE","year":2026},{"abstract":"Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have demonstrated exceptional performance on graph-structured data. However, their success heavily relies on the availability of clean labels, an assumption that often fails in real-world scenarios. The learnability of GCNs is intrinsically linked to the neighborhood structure of nodes, making it critical to understand how this structure changes in the presence of label noise. In this work, we investigate how the neighborhood label distribution of a node changes under label noise. We mathematically derive that label noise smooths this distribution, which inherently increases its entropy and severely decreases interclass distinguishability. To address this challenge, we propose Leave-one-out Entropy Node Screening (LENS), an end-to-end framework that identifies noisy nodes by measuring the reduction in neighborhood entropy when a specific node is removed. LENS further incorporates a relabeling mechanism to recover and preserve valuable feature information instead of entirely discarding the identified noisy nodes. Crucially, the end-to-end computational overhead of LENS is remarkably low. To embed superpixels, current encoders crop them to bounding boxes and then pad, resize, or mask them, so background or fill values can leak into the node features. This matters in practice, and especially in medical imaging, where a prediction should depend on the tissue and not on an arbitrary preprocessing choice: on BACH, changing only the fill of the masked region shifts the accuracy of frozen encoders by up to 6 percentage points, larger than the differences among the four best encoders under mean fill, and the preferred fill differs between datasets, so it cannot be fixed once and for all. We present TAN (Tissue-Aware Network), a compact convolutional encoder (0.41M parameters) that processes each superpixel at its native shape and extent and excludes background from every operation, which makes its embeddings exactly invariant to the fill by construction. Under identical masks and an identical graph classifier, TAN's accuracy on BACH is not significantly different from that of the 303M-parameter foundation model UNI (81.1% vs. 80.7-82.6%, depending on the fill), with ~740x fewer parameters, ~1,190x fewer FLOPs, and no pretraining. On BRACS, TAN is close to a ResNet18 trained under the same protocol and trails the histopathology foundation models. An ablation with TAN's architecture but standard processing of fill-padded crops shows that masking keeps accuracy similar (nominally higher on BACH, lower on BRACS, within noise) at less than half the FLOPs.","already_present":false,"authors":["Jan Herschel","A. von Gladiss"],"candidate_id":"candidate-982bfe400a683d3b22e684c2","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.23475","semantic_scholar":"886d28e9d078a546083945e7c9dc3196c9966cf7"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.23475","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/886d28e9d078a546083945e7c9dc3196c9966cf7","title":"TAN: A Size- and Form-Adaptive Masked-Convolution Encoder for Tissue Graphs","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Train delay heterogeneity between service categories is well known but rarely characterized at large scale from operational data, and rarely used directly to drive the design of graph-based delay-propagation models. This study uses the real International Railway Network Dataset (IRD2025) – 2,678,291 operational records from 3,324 trains across 1,397 stations on the Italian railway network, January–June 2024 – to empirically characterize this delay heterogeneity and to motivate and evaluate a heterogeneous graph-based delay-prediction framework (HTW-STGN).\n \n \n \n Exploratory analysis is conducted on the full real IRD2025 dataset, rather than the smaller synthetic validation sample used in earlier work, to characterize delay heterogeneity across the seven Italian train service categories and to test the empirical assumptions – cross-category delay correlation, weather sensitivity and category-level delay ranking – that originally motivated the heterogeneous-edge design of HTW-STGN. HTW-STGN is implemented as a relation-aware graph-feature aggregation model, with heterogeneous edges (same-category/cross-category) grounded in real, physically observed infrastructure sharing and evaluated on a held-out June 2024 test set.\n \n \n \n Results confirm and correct earlier reported patterns: regional services (96.4% of all records) have lower delays than long-distance categories, the opposite of the result reported from the earlier synthetic sample; the weather effect is real but moderate rather than strongly multiplicative as earlier estimated; and cross-category delay correlation is consistently weak (r = −0.05 to 0.37) rather than the high correlation (up to 0.89) that had originally motivated the choice of heterogeneous graph edges. Only 4.6% of station-to-station links in the network are used by more than one train category, and this real infrastructure-sharing structure – rather than delay correlation – is used to root HTW-STGN's heterogeneous edges. This design reduces mean absolute delay-prediction error by 12% beyond a homogeneous-graph baseline (95% CI [0.49, 0.63] min, p < 0.001) and by approximately 40% beyond features that ignore graph structure entirely, consistently across all seven categories.\n \n \n \n This is the first large-scale empirical characterization of delay heterogeneity across the full real Italian Railway Network Dataset, and the first to test – and correct – the correlational assumptions behind a heterogeneous graph-based delay-propagation architecture using real operational data rather than a synthetic proxy. HTW-STGN's heterogeneous-edge design is re-grounded in observed infrastructure sharing rather than delay correlation, offering a first empirical test of the heterogeneous-edge hypothesis for delay propagation in Italian railways.","already_present":false,"authors":["K. Graph neural networks (GNNs) rely on message passing over these edges, making relational privacy protection a critical concern. To mitigate privacy risks, edge-level differential privacy (DP) has been widely adopted to perturb graph structures. However, existing edge-level DP mechanisms apply uniform perturbation across all edges, disregarding their heterogeneous structural importance. To address this limitation, we propose a personalized edge-level privacy-preserving GNN (PELP-GNN) learning framework, the first personalized edge-level privacy-preserving GNN learning framework, whose key novelty is to assign each edge a differentiated privacy budget according to its structural significance, thereby avoiding the overprotection of low-importance edges and the underprotection of critical ones. Specifically, PELP-GNN estimates edge importance based on forest edge centrality (FEC) and allocates personalized privacy budgets accordingly. Furthermore, it incorporates an adaptive aggregation scheme to mitigate the effects of nonuniform noise during message passing. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that PELP-GNN satisfies $\\epsilon $ -edge local DP (LDP) while providing personalized protection. Unlike existing works, PELP-GNN is a general, plug-and-play framework that can be seamlessly integrated into state-of-the-art edge-level DP-based GNN learning frameworks. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy across varying privacy budgets.","already_present":false,"authors":["Zi-Jun Song","Dian Lei","Yan-Li Yuan","Lie-Huang Zhu"],"candidate_id":"candidate-23f5d8307d957e5da1d08b7c","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.1109/jiot.2026.3721975","semantic_scholar":"0dab363602973fe3d7a9d49f3f2f47a6dd9694e4"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1109/jiot.2026.3721975","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/0dab363602973fe3d7a9d49f3f2f47a6dd9694e4","title":"Achieving Personalized Edge-Level Privacy-Preserving Graph Neural Networks on Decentralized Graphs","venue":"IEEE Internet of Things Journal","year":2026},{"abstract":"Cooperative localization (CL) is a key enabler for future cooperative intelligent transportation system applications. By sharing and fusing multisource information, it can provide high-accuracy localization for connected autonomous vehicles in GNSS-denied or limited environments. Practical CL scenarios often involve heterogeneous cooperative nodes, such as vehicles and landmarks, and relative measurements (e.g., range and bearing). However, existing graph neural network (GNN)-based CL methods do not sufficiently account for scene heterogeneity or fully exploit relative information. Moreover, the state components estimated in CL exhibit substantial scale discrepancies, making effective joint optimization crucial for improving the overall estimation performance of the model. To address these issues, a heterogeneous CL Graph Transformer (HCLGT), together with an adaptive optimization strategy, is proposed for the real-vehicle CL task. First, we incorporate edge-based relative position encoding into the attention computation to better leverage relative measurements. Second, we design relation-specific aggregation modules for different measurement relationships and employ node uncertainty to adaptively adjust attention weights, improving robustness under heterogeneous information quality. Finally, an adaptive loss function is developed to dynamically balance the optimization of multiscale state components. The proposed method is validated on the real-world Leibniz University Cooperative Perception and Urban Navigation Dataset (LUCOOP). Experimental results show that, compared with the best-performing baseline, the proposed method reduces the localization RMSE by 44.61%. Extensive experimental analyses further validate the effectiveness of each module.","already_present":false,"authors":["Sheng-Sheng Xing","Hai-Gen Min","Xia Wu","Wu-Qi Wang","Xiang-Mo Zhao","Guo-Qiang Mao"],"candidate_id":"candidate-1759d0ab90fd511ada8523ff","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.1109/jiot.2026.3720786","semantic_scholar":"dc5cc46d1ade8958a153b1c27d278a58760b3dbe"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1109/jiot.2026.3720786","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/dc5cc46d1ade8958a153b1c27d278a58760b3dbe","title":"Heterogeneous Graph Transformer for Connected Autonomous Vehicles' Cooperative Localization","venue":"IEEE Internet of Things Journal","year":2026},{"abstract":"Longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) contain complementary diagnostic and laboratory information about patient health. However, irregularity, sparsity, heterogeneity, and incompleteness in documentation complicate EHR modeling. To address the problem, we introduce GraphBEAT (Graph-based Bucketized Event Aggregation over Time), a temporal graph representation learning framework that groups clinical events into time buckets and transforms observed features into patient-specific, temporally directed graphs to enable early risk stratification for gastrointestinal cancers. Each node in an EHR graph encodes feature identity, observed value, and temporal position of clinical events. A context-aware, time-decay message-passing mechanism models transitions between successive buckets, followed by multi-head attention pooling to generate patient-level representations. GraphBEAT was trained and evaluated on multi-site longitudinal diagnosis codes and laboratory tests to predict pancreatic, liver, and intestinal cancer at 12-, 24-, and 36-month diagnostic lead times. In all experimental setups, GraphBEAT consistently outperformed baseline graph neural networks (GraphSAGE, GAT, and GCN) and sequence modeling approaches (Transformer and long short-term memory [LSTM]). GraphBEAT also required over 250x fewer floating-point operations per patient and over 20x fewer parameters than the Transformer and LSTM baselines. These results support GraphBEAT as an accurate and computationally efficient approach for cancer risk stratification from sparse, heterogeneous longitudinal health records.","already_present":false,"authors":["L. Salehinejad"],"candidate_id":"candidate-018eb36afc1f4c731eeda5f8","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.22014","semantic_scholar":"39643ba8a6fdacf83012ef762eb8e078aafdb07b"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.22014","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/39643ba8a6fdacf83012ef762eb8e078aafdb07b","title":"GraphBEAT: Graph-based Bucketized Event Aggregation Over Time for Early Risk Stratification of Gastrointestinal Cancers","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Grid foundation models (GridFMs) are graph transformers pretrained on a masked power-flow objective, and evaluate power flow orders of magnitude faster than an iterative solver. Their size, however, targets data-centre inference, whereas low-inertia operation increasingly asks for inference at the edge, next to the measurement, at batch size one and within a single synchrophasor (PMU) reporting frame. We distil a 20.1M-parameter, 12-layer GridFM teacher into a 0.62M-parameter, 6-layer student, a $32.5\\times$ parameter reduction at half the message-passing depth, using an objective that combines the masked power-flow loss with output, physics-residual, latent-state and attention transfer. The physics-residual term, which matches the teacher's power-residual profile, has not previously been applied to typed power-grid graphs. We evaluate on a renewable variant of the IEEE 118-bus benchmark grid in which 26 of the conventional (synchronous) generators are replaced by inverter-based renewables with battery flexibility and standardised reactive-power limits (IEEE 1547), giving $97\\,529$ physically valid (AC-OPF-feasible) operating scenarios, and we ablate all eight combinations of the transfer terms, reporting accuracy against ground truth and fidelity to the teacher separately. Distillation lowers student error on all four predicted quantities, by up to $48\\%$ on active-power dispatch, and every distilled student is more accurate than its teacher on reactive-power dispatch. The gain is largely carried by the output matching term. Despite communication encryption, app fingerprinting (AF) attacks can still enable adversaries to infer the apps in use by analyzing patterns of encrypted network traffic. Existing sheaf architectures, however, define the sheaf Laplacian as an instantaneous spatial operator and therefore cannot explicitly model how signals evolve over time on a graph. We first introduce a spectral sheaf Laplacian, defined jointly over space and time, such that a single operator regulates signal propagation across both the spatial graph and the temporal domain. In class-incremental graph learning, predictions are often dominated by recently learned classes, causing severe recency bias. Dynamic expansion can isolate knowledge across sessions, but many methods assume task-incremental settings and require task identities at test time to select branches or heads---information unavailable in class-incremental learning. Learnable routers offer an alternative, yet continual fine-tuning the router on new data can bias routing toward recent components. We propose MAEM, a replay-free, capacity-controlled dynamic mixture-of-experts framework for class-incremental graph learning. MAEM builds representations with Simplified Graph Convolution (SGC) and trains a dedicated expert for each new session, then freezes it to protect prior knowledge. For routing without task IDs or a shared trainable router, each expert uses a masked autoencoder (MAE); test nodes are assigned to the expert with the lowest reconstruction error, reducing routing-level recency bias. When the expert pool reaches a fixed capacity, MAEM merges the least-used experts via Git Re-Basin alignment and further distills them into a fused expert using topology-aware pseudo data synthesized from MAE distributions (DeepInversion-style), without storing or revisiting historical graph data. It is a disease with an often asymptomatic onset, which means that a high percentage of affected individuals remain unidentified until quite far in the disease process, thereby underlining the importance of a good, reliable screening instrument for proactive detection. In this paper, GlucoSense is introduced as a single framework for early NIDDM risk stratification by combining Human Activity Recognition (HAR) with continuous blood glucose forecasting using two Graph Attention Network version 2 (GATv2)-based architectures. The first is a HAR module trained with smartphone triaxial accelerometer data that covers 23 activity classes, while the second is a glucose prediction module trained with the OhioT1DM dataset to predict glucose levels for a 30 min horizon. Unlike sequential models, GlucoSense encodes complex dependencies between movement patterns, cardiac activity, nutrition, and glycemic behaviour by modeling relationships in a graph structure. The study was longitudinal, spanning 90 days, with six participants. Three important clinical parameters, mean glucose level, time above hyperglycemic level, and glycemic coefficient of variance were calculated. The system was able to correctly identify metabolically healthy individuals and those with prediabetic patterns. The framework was cross-validated with HbA1c laboratory tests to verify the clinical consistency of the framework. Both modules were benchmarked against sequential, convolutional, attention-based, and graph-based baselines under an identical protocol with five independent runs. The glucose module lowered the root mean squared error from 31.82 mg/dL for an LSTM baseline to 25.60 mg/dL, and the activity module reached 98.50% accuracy, with every difference confirmed by paired significance testing and reported with 95% confidence intervals. However, recent studies have revealed their vulnerability to adversarial attacks, where imperceptible perturbations to the graph structure can easily mislead predictions. Existing defense methods predominantly rely on global heuristic strategies, which often lead to over-smoothing in deep architectures and fail to capture localized, fine-grained structural anomalies. In this paper, we propose Topology-Aware Dynamic Co-evolution (TADC), a novel framework that reformulates graph defense as a closed-loop optimization process. Unlike static purification paradigms, TADC introduces a closed-loop dynamic co-evolution framework, in which graph topology and model parameters are jointly optimized through validation-guided meta-gradients, enabling continuous and adaptive structural refinement during training. To further ensure the reliability of topology updates, we identify the topology-agnostic limitation of conventional meta-gradients and propose a topology-aware gradient calibration mechanism, which incorporates structural priors to guide gradient directions toward more plausible and semantically consistent graph modifications. Concretely, TADC first localizes vulnerable nodes via a structural-semantic consistency probe and constructs an initialized graph through topology-aware refinement. It then performs structure decoupling to disentangle reliable and potentially adversarial edges into distinct channels. Under the message-passing framework, mainstream GNN models alternate between feature transformation and neighborhood aggregation. Prior fusion accelerators fall short of this target in three ways: designs that gather the raw input features for aggregation or write transformed features off-chip incur redundant traffic, designs that stream transformed features on-chip still keep the two phases as separate matrix kernels without a unified execution granularity, and the designs that aggregate at message granularity serialize per-destination aggregation or allocate state that does not scale to large graphs. This issue exacerbates passenger waiting times, creates load imbalances between buses, and undermines service reliability. Reinforcement learning (RL) has proven highly effective for mitigating bus bunching and outperforms traditional model-based approaches. However, existing RL approaches require agents to continuously interact with the environment, which potentially disrupts the bus system before effective policies are learned. This paper proposes an Offline Graph-based Multi-agent Actor-Critic (Offline-GMAC) method that trains bus holding policies using only readily available logged GPS data collected during normal uncontrolled operations, thereby eliminating the need for disruptive online interaction or exploration. The method employs general graph neural networks for multi-agent credit assignment. A key innovation of our method is a data augmentation scheme that synthesizes unperformed holding actions from historical uncontrolled bus trajectories. The scheme exploits the equivalence between stochastic link travel time delays and deliberate holding interventions. Under mild assumptions, we prove that the 1-Wasserstein distance between synthesized and target state transition distributions is bounded above by a term that scales linearly with the standard deviation of link travel times plus a tunable synthesis-dependent term. Evaluations using real-world bus data demonstrate that the proposed offline method achieves performance comparable to, and in some cases, even better than its online counterpart.","already_present":false,"authors":["Min-Yu Shen","Xiao-Wen Bi","Wei-Hua Gu","Zhan-Dong Xu","Yue-Zhong Wu","Feng Xiao","Lu Li"],"candidate_id":"candidate-60162263b047812103b1c381","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.14632","semantic_scholar":"e45216ee795bfa3f900ea5a00adb8d4a73110045"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.14632","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/e45216ee795bfa3f900ea5a00adb8d4a73110045","title":"From Observation to Intervention: Mastering Bus Holding Control from Historical Uncontrolled Trajectories with Offline Reinforcement Learning","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Multi-robot systems (MRS) offer significant advantages over single-robot platforms by enabling information sharing and coordination for different tasks in complex environments. However, reliable cooperation critically depends on inferring trust over both information sources and their reported hypotheses, particularly under partial observability and potential adversarial interference. Existing approaches frequently depend on pre-established trust relationships or side-channel information, which may not be available or reliable in realistic MRS deployments. This work introduces NeST-Bayes, a neural-symbolic framework that jointly infers robot and hypothesis trust using only inter-robot observation consistency, without requiring preassigned robot trust, reputation information, or side-channel identity signals. NeST-Bayes infers instantaneous trust evidence scores for robots and object hypotheses by reasoning over ego-centric relational graphs constructed from cross-robot observation consistency. These evidence scores are accumulated over time through Bayesian updates of Beta-distributed trust beliefs to maintain temporally consistent trust estimates. Extensive evaluations show that NeST-Bayes achieves the highest mean object precision and robot recall across all benchmark settings, and the highest robot precision and object recall in most settings, compared to trust-based methods. Under aggressive optimized attacks, it achieves 98.8\\% robot precision with 93.8\\% recall and 98.3\\% object precision with 95.4\\% recall. In an occlusion-rich Webots warehouse, it maintains 92.5\\% robot precision with 92.0\\% recall and 97.3\\% object precision with 85.0\\% recall. We formulate this as seed-conditioned response ranking: given a perturbation at one seed node, ranking all other nodes by response strength. This is challenging when the model is given only the interaction topology, while the mechanism governing how perturbations propagate must be learned from data. We present VQIL (Visible Quantum Interference Learning), a trainable Szegedy quantum walk for seed-conditioned ranking. Edge weights, link phases, and per-node phase rotations are optimized end-to-end by backpropagation while the walk operator remains unitary throughout training. Node scores are obtained from a geometrically discounted coherent sum of quantum-walk amplitudes, enabling quantum interference before the final squared-norm readout. Because each learned parameter is attached to a named edge or node, the trained model provides directly inspectable hypotheses about the roles of individual graph components in the propagation mechanism. On AC power-flow perturbations over six transmission grids, with electrical parameters withheld from the model, VQIL improves Spearman rank correlation from 0.147 for the untrained walk to 0.831 and outperforms an identically trained random-walk model. On gene perturbation over five protein-protein interaction networks with Perturb-seq supervision, VQIL improves rank correlation from 0.171 to 0.620, outperforming the strongest learned classical and neural baselines. These results show that trainable quantum-walk interference provides a scalable and interpretable inductive bias for learning seed-conditioned response rankings on graphs.","already_present":false,"authors":["Seokjun Lee","Sergio Ortega","Daniel K. However, conventional graphs are inherently limited to pairwise connections and are less effective at representing group-wise coordination patterns in human motion, where multiple joints often act as a functional unit during complex movements such as swinging or throwing. Hypergraphs provide a natural alternative by allowing hyperedges to connect arbitrary numbers of joints and explicitly encode coordinated joint groups. We propose the Motion-Guided Channel-Wise Hypergraph Convolutional Network (MC-HGCN), which models skeleton sequences through a unified hypergraph structure with three complementary mechanisms. MC-HGCN first constructs anatomical body-part and cross-limb hyperedges to provide structural priors. A motion-guided modulation mechanism adaptively reweights the hypergraph incidence matrix according to per-frame joint motion intensity, dynamically emphasizing active joint groups. Furthermore, a channel-wise hyperedge learning module discovers distinct coordination patterns across feature channels, enabling feature-specific relational modeling. A residual pathway preserves fine-grained pairwise information to complement high-order hypergraph aggregation. Extensive experiments on NTU RGB+D 60 and NTU RGB+D 120 demonstrate that MC-HGCN achieves strong performance using only joint coordinates, with notable improvements on high-motion actions involving complex multi-joint coordination. The hazard level of urban patrol cases can be reflected by the urgency level and prioritizing high-urgency cases can help reduce potential risks to public safety. However, it remains challenging to assess the urgency level of urban patrol cases when reliable urgency labels are limited or unavailable. To address this problem, this paper proposes an urban patrol case urgency classification method based on self-supervised clustering of a graph neural network. First, a case-relationship graph is constructed from urban patrol cases. A graph attention-based autoencoder is then pretrained to learn node representations, and K-means is used to initialize cluster centers. Finally, representation learning and clustering are jointly optimized to identify urgency-oriented clusters without using manual labels during training. Experimental validation was conducted using 6126 urban patrol case records from Zhengzhou, China. The proposed method achieved a Recall of 0.7458, Precision of 0.7465, ACC of 0.7424, F1 of 0.7403, and NMI of 0.4517. Compared with TADW, the strongest baseline, the proposed method improved these metrics by 0.0617, 0.0479, 0.0650, 0.0690, and 0.0407, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively learn urgency-related latent representations and improve the classification quality of urban patrol cases.","already_present":false,"authors":["Yi-Rui Jiang","Hao Wu","Tie-Jun Yang","Jia-Yu Sun","Hong-Wei Li","Wen-Jie Zhu"],"candidate_id":"candidate-86fd684e23a2bf72f9dda4c7","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.1371/journal.pone.0360432","semantic_scholar":"f6dfbbea43d29a2b7a5d15650a6448a6772825ec"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0360432","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/f6dfbbea43d29a2b7a5d15650a6448a6772825ec","title":"An urban patrol case urgency classification method based on self-supervised clustering of a graph neural network","venue":"PLoS ONE","year":2026},{"abstract":"The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based maritime surveillance is becoming an important part of maritime Internet of Things (IoT) and intelligent transportation systems. It provides a flexible and cost-effective way to large-scale maritime traffic monitoring. However, achieving robust situational awareness remains challenging in practical maritime environments. The main challenges arise from heterogeneous sensing modalities, adverse imaging conditions, and spatial misalignment caused by UAV motion. To address these problems, this paper proposes an airborne multi-modal graph learning-driven framework, termed AMGT, for vessel identification and tracking in UAV-assisted maritime IoT. Specifically, visible and infrared images are first aligned and fused through a multi-parameter perspective transformation model. This improves visual perception under low visibility and complex illumination conditions. Automatic identification system (AIS) messages are then temporally synchronized using interpolation and linear prediction. To detect small and oriented vessels, we develop a mixed-modality MAir-YOLOv8-OBB detector, followed by the MAir-SORT algorithm for stable vessel tracking. We further design a graph learning-driven association network to model temporal dynamics and spatial dependencies among vessels and between vessels and UAVs. A motion-aware coordinate unification (MCU) strategy is also introduced to reduce nonlinear misalignment caused by UAV motion. Experiments on the MAP-M2UAV50 dataset show that AMGT achieves high accuracy and efficiency. The results demonstrate its potential for UAV-assisted maritime IoT applications, including vessel monitoring, traffic situational awareness, and intelligent maritime transportation services. The dataset and code will be available at https://github.com/MAPGroup/AMGT.","already_present":false,"authors":["Chen-Jie Zhao","Jiang-Tian Nie","Jia-Wen Kang","Yu-Xu Lu","Ryan Wen Liu"],"candidate_id":"candidate-d97bc937a2b8045ccddb613b","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.13220","doi":"10.1109/jiot.2026.3741844","semantic_scholar":"4cfd38457030895b0f6313e7e1110d9e67a33f10"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1109/jiot.2026.3741844","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/4cfd38457030895b0f6313e7e1110d9e67a33f10","title":"Multi-Modal Graph Neural Network-Inspired Vessel Identification and Tracking for UAV-Based Maritime Surveillance","venue":"IEEE Internet of Things Journal","year":2026},{"abstract":"In navigating the challenges of computational and communication overhead within the 6G-era Collaborative Inference (CI), this paper explores the feasibility of employing Stacked Intelligent Metasurface (SIM) to perform CI, termed SIM-CI. The SIM functions as a physical computing unit, receiving multi-user Over-The-Air (OTA) aggregated features within the same spectrum. It thus executes the necessary spatial-frequency combining and inference in a single physical wave propagation.SIM-CI also incorporates a tri-heterogeneity robustness adapter to address the network heterogeneity, such as multi-modal data and user inference models, as well as a quality-aware contrastive approach that align features from different modalities and extraction levels into a unified feature space. This formulation enables the model to resolve logical inconsistencies and rectify unreliable connections, producing robust discrete topology graphs that closely approach theoretical maximum performance. candidates.abstract: With the development of the integration of aerial, terrestrial, and satellite networks, Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) serve as a new type of aerial communication platform, playing a key role in Internet of Things (IoT) scenarios. However, multi-hop UAV networks still suffer from energy limits, bandwidth scarcity, dynamic topology, and unstable links. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an edge-cloud communication protocol framework (EC-LLM-MARL) based on Large Language Models (LLMs) and MARL. In this framework, the cloud side constructs a chain-of-thought to guide LLM reasoning, and distilled expert strategies are transferred to UAVs through knowledge distillation and fine-tuning, improving training efficiency and reducing communication overhead. Additionally, a Graph Attention Network (GAT) is employed to extract deep features of observation targets, while Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) is combined with a self-attention mechanism at the UAV end to enhance credit assignment and convergence efficiency in dynamic environments. Furthermore, the framework designs a differentiated reward mechanism for task load balancing among multiple UAVs, improving the scalability of the algorithm in large-scale network scenarios. Extensive simulations show that EC-LLM-MARL significantly accelerates training convergence and substantially outperforms existing methods, achieving a 77% increase in throughput, a 13% rise in coverage, and the highest remaining energy levels.
candidates.title: LLM-Enhanced MARL for Multi-Hop UAV Networking: An Edge-Cloud Protocol Aware Framework

candidates.abstract: Person Re-IDentification (ReID) is vital for public-safety applications, yet camera-based ReID suffers in low-light environments and poses serious visual privacy risks. In contrast, millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar sensing has gained significant attention in ReID due to its ability to perceive human movement patterns by emitting electromagnetic waves, making ReID unaffected by lighting conditions and capable of privacy preserving. However, current radar-based ReID methods are primarily supervised, and radar data is challenging for human eyes to interpret, making annotation extremely difficult and costly. To this end, we propose an unsupervised radar ReID method based on multi-level cross-view mutual signal contrastive learning. First, to drive unsupervised contrastive learning that depends on data augmentations, we utilize signal processing techniques to transform raw radar signals into frequency spectrum and point clouds, and these forms constitute different and complementary augmented versions of the same sample. Second, we construct a multi-level contrastive model between frequency spectrum signals and point clouds through global contrast, cross-view prediction contrast, clustering contrast, and cross-view cluster center contrast, effectively aligning different views and enhancing unsupervised robustness. Additionally, we employ a well-designed local and global graph attention network to learn more discriminative radar point cloud features. Extensive experimental results illustrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing radar-based unsupervised methods.
candidates.title: mmWave Radar-Based Unsupervised Person ReID via Multi-Level Mutual Signal Contrastive Learning

candidates.abstract: With the rapid advancement of mobile technology and ubiquitous computing, spatial crowdsourcing has emerged as a promising computing paradigm. The growing complexity of spatial tasks has increasingly driven the demand for coordination among interdependent tasks and the cooperative participation of mobile workers, which remains relatively unexplored among existing studies. To fill this gap, this paper introduces Dependency-Cooperative Spatial Crowdsourcing (DCSC), a novel problem that explicitly models task dependencies and enables systematic worker cooperation to address complex spatial scenarios. To solve DCSC, we propose a two-stage solution: Dependency-aware Recommendation and Cooperation-aware Matching. In the first stage, we develop a multi-agent reinforcement learning approach enhanced with meta-gradient techniques to recommend suitable subtasks while considering dependency constraints. In the second stage, we propose a genetic algorithm-enhanced game approach to achieve optimal cooperative assignment, guided by a multi-dimensional matching utility function. To ensure consistency and optimization across both stages, we employ meta-gradients from the policy network to guide the optimization of the utility function. Additionally, we utilize graph neural network-based policy clustering to address task heterogeneity, enabling each cluster to learn specialized parameters and enhance reinforcement learning performance. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of our approach.
candidates.title: Efficient Task Assignment in Dependency-Cooperative Spatial Crowdsourcing

candidates.abstract: Addressing distribution shifts between training and testing sets is paramount for Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). Graph rationale learning has emerged as an effective paradigm to tackle this challenge by extracting invariant subgraphs as rationales for prediction. However, existing methods typically rely on the subgraphs produced by a rationale extractor without explicitly assessing their reliability, particularly during early training stages when the extractor is prone to generating inaccurate or biased rationales. Learning with such unreliable rationales can mislead the classifier and further deteriorate rationale quality, ultimately undermining generalization performance. In this paper, we rethink the objective of graph rationale learning and propose Cooperative Rationale Selection (CoRas), a novel architecture designed to enhance the reliability and robustness of rationale representations. Specifically, CoRas employs a dual-classifier framework to cooperatively select reliable rationales. Motivated by the small-loss criterion, CoRas prioritizes rationales with low prediction loss, while simultaneously selecting rationales with high prediction divergence to mitigate selection bias caused by relying solely on self-predictions during training. This allows CoRas to effectively select reliable rationales for downstream tasks, subsequently enhancing graph rationale learning. Experimental results on both real-world benchmarks and synthetic datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of CoRas in extracting reliable rationale subgraphs for combating out-of-distribution graph settings in graph classification.
candidates.title: CoRas: Cooperative Rationale Selection for Graph Rationale Learning in Out-of-Distribution Graphs

candidates.abstract: Modern power grids are increasingly exposed to diverse cyber-physical attacks that originate in the cyber layer and disrupt physical operation. A critical defense challenge is to rapidly determine whether an attack has occurred and identify its type. To address this challenge, this paper aims to develop a generalized detection scheme capable of identifying multiple types of attacks, particularly unknown ones. It is first observed that, under normal operation, cyber-layer data and physical-layer states are consistent across layers and evolve smoothly over time, while attacks disrupt these consistencies. Building on this insight, a self-supervised Cross-Layer Cross-Temporal Contrastive Learning (CL-CTCL) framework is proposed, which employs a Graph Attention Network-Gated Recurrent Unit (GAT-GRU) encoder to capture spatial dependencies and temporal dynamics. Two complementary contrastive objectives are introduced: Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization (VICReg) for cross-layer alignment and Information Noise-Contrastive Estimation with Momentum Contrast (InfoNCE-MoCo) for temporal consistency. Residual deviations from these consistencies provide reliable attack fingerprints, enabling detection and classification of both known and unknown attacks. Experiments on an IEEE 118-bus cyber-physical testbed show that the proposed CL-CTCL achieves high accuracy on known attacks and generalizes well to unknown ones, outperforming baseline methods across standard metrics.
candidates.title: Detection of Unknown Attack in Cyber–Physical Power Systems via Self-Supervised Cross-Layer and Cross-Temporal Consistency

candidates.abstract: Deep learning (DL)-based methods have illustrated excellent performance in distribution network fault diagnosis. However, the “opaque” nature of DL models hinders grid operators from understanding the decision-making processes of these models, affecting model trustworthiness and robustness in diversified diagnosis applications. This paper proposes a hybrid attention-augmented self-interpretable channel-grouped graph convolutional network (HASIG) for diverse short-circuit fault diagnosis of distribution networks, including binary fault detection, faulted line identification, and fault type classification. A channel-grouped graph convolutional network is proposed to learn features from three-phase voltage and current measurements. We present a hybrid attention that combines global edge attention and channel-grouped attention, which can augment the critical features with faithful and robust interpretations during model training, enabling users to gain insights into the predictive behavior inside the model. These three short-circuit fault diagnosis tasks are collaboratively trained under a multi-task learning architecture with interpretable loss constraints. Experiments were conducted on the IEEE 33-bus, IEEE 33-bus with distributed energy resources, and IEEE 123-bus systems with randomized fault parameters. The results show that HASIG achieves competitive diagnostic performance and good interpretability, and demonstrates strong robustness under noisy and missing-data conditions.
candidates.title: Hybrid Attention-Augmented Self-Interpretable Channel-Grouped Graph Convolutional Network for Robust Distribution Network Fault Diagnosis

candidates.abstract: This work addresses a fundamental challenge in applying deep learning to network topology-dependent power system applications: developing neural network models that transfer across significant system changes, including networks with entirely different topologies and dimensionalities, without requiring training data from unseen reconfigurations. We focus on situational awareness tasks where predictions inherently depend on network-wide spatial relationships through electrical connectivity. Despite extensive research, most ML-based approaches remain system-specific, limiting real-world deployment. This limitation stems from a dual barrier. First, topology changes shift feature distributions and alter input dimensions due to power flow physics. Second, reconfigurations redefine output semantics and dimensionality, requiring models to handle configuration-specific outputs while maintaining transferable feature extraction. Our core insight is treating topology as a learnable dimension through training on diverse reconfigurations, enabling the model to learn universal power flow physics rather than memorizing fixed networks. We achieve this through three synergistic mechanisms: scalar-weight graph convolutions with physics-aware operators handle variable input dimensions and distribution shifts, adaptive pooling maps topology-specific features to unified latent representations, and parallel transformer generates configuration-specific outputs using positional encoding. Our Universal Graph Convolutional Network (UGCN) achieves transferability to any reconfiguration or variation of existing power systems without any prior knowledge of new grid topologies or retraining during implementation. Experimental results on state forecasting and false data injection detection demonstrate that UGCN significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in cross-system zero-shot transferability across both transmission and distribution networks.
candidates.title: Universal Graph Convolutional Network: Zero-Shot Transfer Across Power Grid Topology Reconfigurations

candidates.abstract: Graph-structured representations of text data have become foundational across machine learning, yet it remains unclear how to systematically construct a graph from a given dataset for a target task. Choices about which entities become nodes, which relationships become edges, and what text each node contains can substantially affect downstream performance. In practice, finding optimal constructions often requires expert knowledge or manual trial and error. We introduce TACO-Graph, a decision tree framework for learning which graph construction choices are most effective for a given dataset and task. Specifically, we focus on text-attributed graphs (TAGs) constructed from multi-attribute tabular data. TACO-Graph enumerates valid TAG representations, scores each using fast proxy evaluation on small representative subsets, and trains an interpretable decision tree on those scores. Across five datasets spanning citation networks, product reviews, and bibliographic relationships, our decision trees predict construction quality on separately drawn evaluation samples with mean Spearman $\rho$ above $0.9$ for node classification and above $0.8$ for GraphRAG retrieval. Our trees systematically identify which constructions perform better across both GNN and GraphRAG tasks, and the full pipeline is released as an open-source library to support evaluation on new tasks and datasets at https://github.com/AmiriHayes/text_attributed_graphs. TACO-Graph provides a systematic and interpretable guide for determining how to convert tabular data to text-attributed graphs for downstream tasks.
candidates.title: TACO-Graph: Automated Construction of Text-Atributed Graphs
