candidates.title: TAN: A Size- and Form-Adaptive Masked-Convolution Encoder for Tissue Graphs

candidates.abstract:
Train delay heterogeneity between service categories is well known but rarely characterized at large scale from operational data, and rarely used directly to drive the design of graph-based delay-propagation models. This study uses the real International Railway Network Dataset (IRD2025) – 2,678,291 operational records from 3,324 trains across 1,397 stations on the Italian railway network, January–June 2024 – to empirically characterize this delay heterogeneity and to motivate and evaluate a heterogeneous graph-based delay-prediction framework (HTW-STGN).
 
 
 
 Exploratory analysis is conducted on the full real IRD2025 dataset, rather than the smaller synthetic validation sample used in earlier work, to characterize delay heterogeneity across the seven Italian train service categories and to test the empirical assumptions – cross-category delay correlation, weather sensitivity and category-level delay ranking – that originally motivated the heterogeneous-edge design of HTW-STGN. HTW-STGN is implemented as a relation-aware graph-feature aggregation model, with heterogeneous edges (same-category/cross-category) grounded in real, physically observed infrastructure sharing and evaluated on a held-out June 2024 test set.
 
 
 
 Results confirm and correct earlier reported patterns: regional services (96.4% of all records) have lower delays than long-distance categories, the opposite of the result reported from the earlier synthetic sample; the weather effect is real but moderate rather than strongly multiplicative as earlier estimated; and cross-category delay correlation is consistently weak (r = −0.05 to 0.37) rather than the high correlation (up to 0.89) that had originally motivated the choice of heterogeneous graph edges. Only 4.6% of station-to-station links in the network are used by more than one train category, and this real infrastructure-sharing structure – rather than delay correlation – is used to root HTW-STGN's heterogeneous edges. This design reduces mean absolute delay-prediction error by 12% beyond a homogeneous-graph baseline (95% CI [0.49, 0.63] min, p < 0.001) and by approximately 40% beyond features that ignore graph structure entirely, consistently across all seven categories.
 
 
 
 This is the first large-scale empirical characterization of delay heterogeneity across the full real Italian Railway Network Dataset, and the first to test – and correct – the correlational assumptions behind a heterogeneous graph-based delay-propagation architecture using real operational data rather than a synthetic proxy. HTW-STGN's heterogeneous-edge design is re-grounded in observed infrastructure sharing rather than delay correlation, offering a first empirical test of the heterogeneous-edge hypothesis for delay propagation in Italian railways.
candidates.title: Delay heterogeneity in Italian rail network with exploratory analysis and a proposed heterogeneous spatio-temporal graph framework

candidates.abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) interconnects billions of devices that naturally form decentralized graph structures, where edges encode privacy-sensitive interaction patterns. Graph neural networks (GNNs) rely on message passing over these edges, making relational privacy protection a critical concern. To mitigate privacy risks, edge-level differential privacy (DP) has been widely adopted to perturb graph structures. However, existing edge-level DP mechanisms apply uniform perturbation across all edges, disregarding their heterogeneous structural importance. To address this limitation, we propose a personalized edge-level privacy-preserving GNN (PELP-GNN) learning framework, the first personalized edge-level privacy-preserving GNN learning framework, whose key novelty is to assign each edge a differentiated privacy budget according to its structural significance, thereby avoiding the overprotection of low-importance edges and the underprotection of critical ones. Specifically, PELP-GNN estimates edge importance based on forest edge centrality (FEC) and allocates personalized privacy budgets accordingly. Furthermore, it incorporates an adaptive aggregation scheme to mitigate the effects of nonuniform noise during message passing. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that PELP-GNN satisfies $\epsilon $ -edge local DP (LDP) while providing personalized protection. Unlike existing works, PELP-GNN is a general, plug-and-play framework that can be seamlessly integrated into state-of-the-art edge-level DP-based GNN learning frameworks. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy across varying privacy budgets.
candidates.title: Achieving Personalized Edge-Level Privacy-Preserving Graph Neural Networks on Decentralized Graphs

candidates.abstract: Cooperative localization (CL) is a key enabler for future cooperative intelligent transportation system applications. By sharing and fusing multisource information, it can provide high-accuracy localization for connected autonomous vehicles in GNSS-denied or limited environments. Practical CL scenarios often involve heterogeneous cooperative nodes, such as vehicles and landmarks, and relative measurements (e.g., range and bearing). However, existing graph neural network (GNN)-based CL methods do not sufficiently account for scene heterogeneity or fully exploit relative information. Moreover, the state components estimated in CL exhibit substantial scale discrepancies, making effective joint optimization crucial for improving the overall estimation performance of the model. To address these issues, a heterogeneous CL Graph Transformer (HCLGT), together with an adaptive optimization strategy, is proposed for the real-vehicle CL task. First, we incorporate edge-based relative position encoding into the attention computation to better leverage relative measurements. Second, we design relation-specific aggregation modules for different measurement relationships and employ node uncertainty to adaptively adjust attention weights, improving robustness under heterogeneous information quality. Finally, an adaptive loss function is developed to dynamically balance the optimization of multiscale state components. The proposed method is validated on the real-world Leibniz University Cooperative Perception and Urban Navigation Dataset (LUCOOP). Experimental results show that, compared with the best-performing baseline, the proposed method reduces the localization RMSE by 44.61%. Extensive experimental analyses further validate the effectiveness of each module.
candidates.title: Heterogeneous Graph Transformer for Connected Autonomous Vehicles' Cooperative Localization

candidates.abstract: Longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) contain complementary diagnostic and laboratory information about patient health. However, irregularity, sparsity, heterogeneity, and incompleteness in documentation complicate EHR modeling. To address the problem, we introduce GraphBEAT (Graph-based Bucketized Event Aggregation over Time), a temporal graph representation learning framework that groups clinical events into time buckets and transforms observed features into patient-specific, temporally directed graphs to enable early risk stratification for gastrointestinal cancers. Each node in an EHR graph encodes feature identity, observed value, and temporal position of clinical events. A context-aware, time-decay message-passing mechanism models transitions between successive buckets, followed by multi-head attention pooling to generate patient-level representations. GraphBEAT was trained and evaluated on multi-site longitudinal diagnosis codes and laboratory tests to predict pancreatic, liver, and intestinal cancer at 12-, 24-, and 36-month diagnostic lead times. In all experimental setups, GraphBEAT consistently outperformed baseline graph neural networks (GraphSAGE, GAT, and GCN) and sequence modeling approaches (Transformer and long short-term memory [LSTM]). GraphBEAT also required over 250x fewer floating-point operations per patient and over 20x fewer parameters than the Transformer and LSTM baselines. These results support GraphBEAT as an accurate and computationally efficient approach for cancer risk stratification from sparse, heterogeneous longitudinal health records.
candidates.title: GraphBEAT: Graph-based Bucketized Event Aggregation Over Time for Early Risk Stratification of Gastrointestinal Cancers

candidates.abstract: Grid foundation models (GridFMs) are graph transformers pretrained on a masked power-flow objective, and evaluate power flow orders of magnitude faster than an iterative solver. Their size, however, targets data-centre inference, whereas low-inertia operation increasingly asks for inference at the edge, next to the measurement, at batch size one and within a single synchrophasor (PMU) reporting frame. We distil a 20.1M-parameter, 12-layer GridFM teacher into a 0.62M-parameter, 6-layer student, a $32.5\times$ parameter reduction at half the message-passing depth, using an objective that combines the masked power-flow loss with output, physics-residual, latent-state and attention transfer. The physics-residual term, which matches the teacher's power-residual profile, has not previously been applied to typed power-grid graphs. We evaluate on a renewable variant of the IEEE 118-bus benchmark grid in which 26 of the conventional (synchronous) generators are replaced by inverter-based renewables with battery flexibility and standardised reactive-power limits (IEEE 1547), giving $97\,529$ physically valid (AC-OPF-feasible) operating scenarios, and we ablate all eight combinations of the transfer terms, reporting accuracy against ground truth and fidelity to the teacher separately. Distillation lowers student error on all four predicted quantities, by up to $48\%$ on active-power dispatch, and every distilled student is more accurate than its teacher on reactive-power dispatch. The gain is largely carried by the output matching term. The physics-residual term, in the layer-aggregated form used here, is consistently harmful, which we attribute to the spatial averaging it applies to a bus-level residual field. The resulting student is $32.5\times$ smaller in parameter count and has half the message-passing depth, making it a candidate for subsequent edge-device benchmarking.
candidates.title: Physics-Aware Distillation of a Grid Foundation Model for Real-Time Edge Inference

candidates.abstract: Mobile apps have become ubiquitous in daily life. Despite communication encryption, app fingerprinting (AF) attacks can still enable adversaries to infer the apps in use by analyzing patterns of encrypted network traffic. However, existing AF attacks suffer from three critical limitations that hinder their practical effectiveness: (i) the inability to capture app-specific traffic dependencies, rendering traffic fingerprints fragile under dynamic networking conditions; (ii) the neglect of latency and throughput considerations, resulting in inefficient real-time user tracking; and (iii) the incapacity to handle mixed traffic generated by multi-app concurrency. In this paper, we propose MAppPrint, a robust and real-time app fingerprinting framework. MAppPrint introduces a behavior-level traffic fingerprint, i.e., Traffic Behavior Correlation Graph (TBCG), which models app traffic by capturing unit traffic behaviors and their correlations, thereby providing reliable app fingerprints. To enable real-time fingerprinting, MAppPrint incorporates a fingerprint compression algorithm that transforms each TBCG into a compact graph by selectively aggregating redundant information. Furthermore, MAppPrint employs an unsupervised decomposition strategy to disentangle mixed traffic generated by multi-app concurrency, enabling unified identification of both single-app and multi-app traffic. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that MAppPrint achieves 4.9~13.9% improvement in AF precision and 3~6 times improvement in timeliness over state-of-the-art methods. Meanwhile, MAppPrint is robust in dynamic networking conditions, while achieving a throughput of 10.5 GB/s and a prediction latency of 0.68 seconds.
candidates.title: MAppPrint: Robust and Real-time Mobile App Fingerprinting via Traffic Behavior Correlation Graphs

candidates.abstract: Sheaf neural networks generalize graph neural networks by assigning each edge a learned linear restriction map that specifies how the local representations of adjacent nodes relate to one another, thereby mitigating oversmoothing. Existing sheaf architectures, however, define the sheaf Laplacian as an instantaneous spatial operator and therefore cannot explicitly model how signals evolve over time on a graph. We first introduce a spectral sheaf Laplacian, defined jointly over space and time, such that a single operator regulates signal propagation across both the spatial graph and the temporal domain. Directly extending this operator's receptive field in space or time would require increasingly complex sheaf structures. Instead, we propose a spectral filter that expands the effective receptive field along both dimensions without enlarging the underlying sheaf. Building on this operator, we introduce ChronoSheaf, a spatio-temporal sheaf network with two key components. First, Transitional Restriction Maps (TRM) decompose each node's restriction map into a spatial term and two temporal frames that independently control its relation to neighboring nodes at the preceding and following timestep, enabling asymmetric temporal influence. Second, the Dual Spectral Filter (DSF) applies a single bounded-degree polynomial filter with an adaptively estimated spectral radius to the joint spatio-temporal sheaf operator. We validate ChronoSheaf on a diverse set of spatio-temporal forecasting benchmarks, where it outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/ChronoSheaf-1D7D/.
candidates.title: ChronoSheaf: Joint Spatio-Temporal Spectral Filtering on Cellular Sheaves

candidates.abstract: The traditional performance cost accounting model of higher education shows obvious lag in dealing with the dynamic allocation of resources and multidimensional performance evaluation, so it is necessary to integrate data intelligence to improve accounting accuracy and management efficiency. Firstly, based on the data set related to education finance published by the Education Economics Laboratory, a heterogeneous graph modeling mechanism is designed to reconstruct the relationship between multiple node types, including teachers, courses, funds and outputs, and form a dynamic knowledge graph sequence. Secondly, by combining the Graph Attention Network (GAT) with the transformer architecture, a cross-time and cross-type performance cost representation model is constructed to support the teaching expenditure prediction and performance fitting analysis. Finally, an anomaly detection mechanism combining Autoencoder and Local Outlier Factor (AE + LOF) is introduced, and a closed-loop system is formed by optimizing budget allocation based on reinforcement learning strategy network. The results show that the prediction accuracy of the GAT model is better than that of the four baseline methods. In the annual scenario, the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) are reduced by 1.52% and 1.63% respectively, which has stronger error stability. In anomaly detection, the average F1 score of AE + LOF framework reaches 0.907, the false positive rate is controlled within 4.3%, and the sample fluctuation of adaptive institutions is less than 3.6%. In budget optimization experiments, the reinforcement learning policy achieved a ΔPerf/ΔCost of 0.178, with a performance improvement rate of 21.5% under high-performance preference conditions. System tests showed end-to-end latency below 200 ms and self-learning convergence within 18 epochs, with the highest user satisfaction rating in “interactivity.” Under the constraints of the data and simulation conditions of this study, graph-structured modeling and intelligent embedding mechanisms hold the potential to enhance the level of intelligence in performance-based cost accounting.
candidates.title: The analysis of intelligent university performance cost accounting driven by big data

candidates.abstract: Resting-state functional connectivity is widely used in machine learning-based classification of neuropsychiatric disorders. Quantum machine learning models have been proposed for functional connectivity data, but few studies have evaluated them under leave-site-out validation or against matched classical models. We compared six quantum model families with classical ones using identical correlation-derived features across four public cohorts (4,308 subjects). Leave-site-out validation was used for the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE I), ADHD-200 (attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder), and REST-meta-MDD (major depressive disorder) cohorts, while the UCLA Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics (UCLA-CNP) was evaluated using stratified 10-fold cross-validation. The quantum kernel was statistically indistinguishable from a matched classical kernel across all four cohorts, with the average accuracy difference within 1.4 percentage points at 95% confidence. On ABIDE I, a hybrid quantum convolutional network achieved similar accuracy to its classical counterpart (0.645 vs. 0.641), while a trainable quantum kernel exceeded its classical counterpart by 0.064 in area under the curve (AUC). Quantum convolutional networks also achieved higher AUC than their matched classical networks on this cohort and showed smaller train-test gaps on all four cohorts, without an accuracy gain. Overall, most quantum models matched their classical counterparts, but none consistently outperformed them. This study, among the first quantum evaluations of ABIDE I under leave-site-out validation, provides a feature-matched benchmark of quantum and classical models comprising 284 matched comparisons. We further analyse fidelity-based graph construction and account for the observed quantum-classical parity through effective-dimension and eigenspectrum analyses.
candidates.title: Quantum Versus Classical Machine Learning for Neuropsychiatric Disorders: A Feature-Matched Multi-Cohort Evaluation

candidates.abstract: The advent of distributional semantics as a framework for computational semantics marked a paradigm shift in the nature of representations, by which meanings are represented as dense vectors commonly known as word embeddings. Computational approaches to historical or typological language comparison, on the other hand, still mostly rely on discrete representations, while the potential of embedding-based methods remains largely untapped in this context. Recent studies have proposed concept embeddings as a language-independent, onomasiological counterpart to word embeddings, based on networks of cross-linguistic colexification patterns. While the resulting concept embeddings reflect meaningful semantic properties and relations, they suffer from a lack of scalability, since they rely on transductive embedding approaches which only learn embeddings for nodes present in the training data. In this study, we present an inductive framework for learning concept embeddings, combining the structural properties of full and partial colexification networks with semantic information from short concept descriptions. This framework allows the embedding of unseen concepts based on a short definition. We show that the resulting concept embeddings correlate with various cross-linguistic measures of similarity or relatedness, while generalizing well to new concepts that were absent from the training data.
candidates.title: Inductive Learning of Concept Embeddings from Cross-Linguistic Colexification Patterns with Textual Attributes

candidates.abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are typically evaluated only at their final layer, obscuring how task-relevant information evolves during message passing. We introduce a post-hoc diagnostic that freezes a trained GNN, fits an independent linear probe to each layer, and tracks probe accuracy alongside normalized predictive entropy. Across real and synthetic graph settings, layer-wise probe entropy distinguishes beneficial, neutral, and harmful smoothing, a capability not demonstrated by existing geometric measures. Moreover, by comparing shallow and deep models, we show that the onset of entropy degradation separates the two main GNN failure modes: structural mismatch under heterophily, which appears from the earliest layers even in shallow models, and excessive-depth oversmoothing, which emerges only as propagation depth increases. These results establish probe-entropy trajectories as a tool for analyzing information flow in GNNs and motivate future work on adaptive depth selection and early-exit mechanisms.
candidates.title: Diagnosing GNN Failure Modes with Layer-Wise Probe Entropy
Edge-Aware Graph Attention Networks for Interpreting Biophysical Mechanisms from Molecular Dynamics Simulations

candidates.abstract: Longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) can reveal disease-progression structure, while useful forecasting requires leakage-controlled discovery, censor-aware outcomes, and inspectable trajectory evidence. We developed a graph-enhanced framework in MIMIC-IV v3.1 that splits patients before graph construction, learns train-only consecutive-admission transitions, and freezes endpoint-specific branching-motif policies selected on validation data. The final catalog contained 99,527 motifs, and a time-aware Transformer retrieved at most 24 patient-compatible motifs per endpoint through endpoint-specific cross-attention. Across five training seeds, micro-AUPRC increased from 0.9330 to 0.9357, while event-time MAE decreased from 676.9 to 657.7 days (reduction 19.2 days; 95% paired patient-cluster bootstrap CI, 13.8-24.8). Timing effects were heterogeneous: MAE worsened for events within 730 days but improved by 58.9 days for events occurring after 730 days. In an exploratory internal temporal split, branch conditioning reduced conditional event-time MAE by 26.9 days (95% CI, 23.0-30.8) without evidence of better micro-AUPRC. Corrected survival evaluation over the supported 0-2,555-day interval did not establish macro C-index or integrated Brier score superiority over a matched history-only discrete-hazard model. A directed, degree-matched GNN repair substantially improved unseen-edge discovery, yet replacing GNN-derived scores within fixed motif identities did not improve downstream forecasting. These results position branching motifs as structured trajectory context whose main value is long-range timing support rather than uniformly stronger endpoint discrimination, survival prediction, or causal explanation.
candidates.title: Graph-Enhanced Disease Trajectory Discovery and Temporal Endpoint Forecasting from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records

candidates.abstract: Architectural technical debt arises when a system's implementation drifts from its inten ded modular decomposition, while the mapping between source files and architectural modu les is missing, incomplete, or costly to maintain manually. We formulate code-to-archite cture mapping as semi-supervised node classification over a directed multi-relational de pendency graph, with files as nodes, typed dependencies as edges, and lexical features d erived from code identifiers and directory layout. Starting from a small labeled sample, an iterative self-training procedure expands the mapping to the remaining files. We com pare a graph convolutional network (GCN), a graph attention network (GAT), and a graph-f ree multi-layer perceptron (MLP), using identical features and training procedures for t he learned models, against a Naive Bayes reference. Across 100 runs on ten open-source J ava and C/C++ systems, all three neural models outperform the reference on both F1 metri cs. GAT achieves the highest averages of system-level median macro and micro F1, at 83.5 and 92.2, respectively, whereas MLP remains competitive or superior on several systems. On Chrome, the largest system with 18,343 files, GAT and GCN exceed MLP by 22 and 19 ma cro-F1 points, respectively, and have substantially fewer persistently misclassified fil es. Connectivity and homophily are associated with where neural message passing helps, w hile multi-relational aggregation outperforms a single merged edge type on every system for both GCN and GAT. A follow-up study finds that several model rankings depend on the training seed, qualifying smaller advantages without removing the large graph benefit ob served on Chrome.
candidates.title: When Does the Dependency Graph Help Code-to-Architecture Mapping?

candidates.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) excel on graph-structured data but suffer catastrophic forgetting when classes arrive sequentially. In class-incremental graph learning, predictions are often dominated by recently learned classes, causing severe recency bias. Dynamic expansion can isolate knowledge across sessions, but many methods assume task-incremental settings and require task identities at test time to select branches or heads---information unavailable in class-incremental learning. Learnable routers offer an alternative, yet continual fine-tuning the router on new data can bias routing toward recent components. We propose MAEM, a replay-free, capacity-controlled dynamic mixture-of-experts framework for class-incremental graph learning. MAEM builds representations with Simplified Graph Convolution (SGC) and trains a dedicated expert for each new session, then freezes it to protect prior knowledge. For routing without task IDs or a shared trainable router, each expert uses a masked autoencoder (MAE); test nodes are assigned to the expert with the lowest reconstruction error, reducing routing-level recency bias. When the expert pool reaches a fixed capacity, MAEM merges the least-used experts via Git Re-Basin alignment and further distills them into a fused expert using topology-aware pseudo data synthesized from MAE distributions (DeepInversion-style), without storing or revisiting historical graph data. On four class-incremental graph benchmarks, MAEM mitigates recency bias, outperforms strong continual graph learning baselines, and keeps model capacity bounded under strict replay-free learning.
candidates.title: MAEM: Mitigating Recency Bias via a Replay-Free, Capacity-Controlled Dynamic Mixture of Experts for Class-Incremental Graph Learning

candidates.abstract: Graph-based analysis of electronic health records (EHRs) yields disease-trajectory catalogs, but structural support does not establish semantic novelty. We present a two-level framework to prioritize 99,527 branching motifs previously discovered by an upstream patient-disjoint, train-only MIMIC-IV v3.1 pipeline and frozen after validation-based catalog selection. The framework separates path-level and node-to-endpoint semantic sparsity from reliability-adjusted clinical priority. Three deterministic textualizations per motif or node-target pair were embedded with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 and calibrated against 166,972 pre-2023 PubMed references using mean top-20 cosine distance. Positive recombination occurred in 8.63% of motifs and had negligible effect on global ranking, whereas specificity and support/GNN reliability terms changed clinical-priority ordering. Robustness analyses across neighbor counts, templates, encoders, generic-label taxonomies, score settings, PrimeKG, and corrected density-based RND showed that broad ordering was more stable than hard top-k membership. A semantic-dose analysis did not support a monotonic relation between score and forecasting benefit after endpoint and token-count adjustment (1.96 days per SD; 95% CI, -0.75 to 4.68). In the frozen catalog-q90 high-semantic subgroup, branch-enhanced forecasting reduced conditional event-time MAE by 20.1 days (95% CI, 13.3-27.0) and sMAPE by 2.37 percentage points (95% CI, 1.81-2.93), while discrimination and endpoint-ranking differences were inconclusive. Corrected RND showed low tail agreement with the primary score (Spearman rho = 0.430; q90 Jaccard = 0.125) despite a similar aggregate timing association. These findings support representation-aware, uncertainty-aware literature-relative prioritization of discovered trajectories rather than causal discovery or clinician-adjudicated novelty.
candidates.title: A Two-Level Clinical Novelty Prioritization Framework for Disease Trajectories Discovered from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records

candidates.abstract: Non-Insulin-Dependent Diabetes Mellitus (NIDDM) is a chronic and progressive metabolic disease characterized by chronically high blood glucose levels. It is a disease with an often asymptomatic onset, which means that a high percentage of affected individuals remain unidentified until quite far in the disease process, thereby underlining the importance of a good, reliable screening instrument for proactive detection. In this paper, GlucoSense is introduced as a single framework for early NIDDM risk stratification by combining Human Activity Recognition (HAR) with continuous blood glucose forecasting using two Graph Attention Network version 2 (GATv2)-based architectures. The first is a HAR module trained with smartphone triaxial accelerometer data that covers 23 activity classes, while the second is a glucose prediction module trained with the OhioT1DM dataset to predict glucose levels for a 30 min horizon. Unlike sequential models, GlucoSense encodes complex dependencies between movement patterns, cardiac activity, nutrition, and glycemic behaviour by modeling relationships in a graph structure. The study was longitudinal, spanning 90 days, with six participants. Three important clinical parameters, mean glucose level, time above hyperglycemic level, and glycemic coefficient of variance were calculated. The system was able to correctly identify metabolically healthy individuals and those with prediabetic patterns. The framework was cross-validated with HbA1c laboratory tests to verify the clinical consistency of the framework. Both modules were benchmarked against sequential, convolutional, attention-based, and graph-based baselines under an identical protocol with five independent runs. The glucose module lowered the root mean squared error from 31.82 mg/dL for an LSTM baseline to 25.60 mg/dL, and the activity module reached 98.50% accuracy, with every difference confirmed by paired significance testing and reported with 95% confidence intervals. Understanding glucose dynamics based on smartphone sensor data and a limited number of physiological markers, GlucoSense offers a non-invasive, scalable and cost-effective alternative to traditional clinical glucose screening. This paper demonstrates the feasibility of smartphone-based longitudinal diabetes risk assessment and motivates future large-scale population studies.
candidates.title: GlucoSense: early diabetes risk assessment via fusion of human activity recognition and glucose prediction

candidates.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have achieved remarkable success in learning from graph-structured data. However, recent studies have revealed their vulnerability to adversarial attacks, where imperceptible perturbations to the graph structure can easily mislead predictions. Existing defense methods predominantly rely on global heuristic strategies, which often lead to over-smoothing in deep architectures and fail to capture localized, fine-grained structural anomalies. In this paper, we propose Topology-Aware Dynamic Co-evolution (TADC), a novel framework that reformulates graph defense as a closed-loop optimization process. Unlike static purification paradigms, TADC introduces a closed-loop dynamic co-evolution framework, in which graph topology and model parameters are jointly optimized through validation-guided meta-gradients, enabling continuous and adaptive structural refinement during training. To further ensure the reliability of topology updates, we identify the topology-agnostic limitation of conventional meta-gradients and propose a topology-aware gradient calibration mechanism, which incorporates structural priors to guide gradient directions toward more plausible and semantically consistent graph modifications. Concretely, TADC first localizes vulnerable nodes via a structural-semantic consistency probe and constructs an initialized graph through topology-aware refinement. It then performs structure decoupling to disentangle reliable and potentially adversarial edges into distinct channels. Building upon this decomposition, a fully differentiable attention-based architecture DeepGCN enables end-to-end optimization of the co-evolution process. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that TADC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various attack settings, with particularly pronounced advantages under strong adversarial perturbations and high perturbation rates. Our code is available at https://github.com/robustgcn/TADC.
candidates.title: Topology-aware dynamic co-evolution for robust graph learning.

candidates.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have become a fundamental tool for learning over graph-structured data. Under the message-passing framework, mainstream GNN models alternate between feature transformation and neighborhood aggregation. Fusing these two phases into a node-level pipelined push dataflow, in which each node’s transformed feature streams directly into aggregation, establishes a single-pass I/O target that reads each input tensor exactly once per layer. No existing hardware sustains this dataflow at full concurrency. Prior fusion accelerators fall short of this target in three ways: designs that gather the raw input features for aggregation or write transformed features off-chip incur redundant traffic, designs that stream transformed features on-chip still keep the two phases as separate matrix kernels without a unified execution granularity, and the designs that aggregate at message granularity serialize per-destination aggregation or allocate state that does not scale to large graphs. We propose PipeGNN, a bandwidth-efficient GNN accelerator whose streaming microarchitecture sustains this dataflow as a fully concurrent pipeline within a fixed on-chip buffer budget. PipeGNN decouples execution from topological boundaries by aligning execution granularity with both memory burst size and aggregation compute throughput, and resolves four coupled microarchitectural barriers through coordinated mechanisms: compute-aligned edge batching, contention-aware message reduction, adaptive cross-batch scheduling, and tiered state residency. Evaluated across diverse GNN workloads, PipeGNN achieves geometric mean speedups of 10.1 × over AWB-GCN and 12.2 × over FlowGNN, and 2.4 × to 46.9 × over a GPU baseline across graph scales, reduces off-chip traffic by 2.69 × over AWB-GCN and 5.93 × over FlowGNN, and improves energy efficiency by 56.81 × over AWB-GCN and 1.53 × over FlowGNN, with a 154 × traffic reduction and a 116.81 × energy reduction against HyGCN.
candidates.title: PipeGNN: A Bandwidth-Efficient GNN Accelerator with Node-Level Pipelined Push Execution
candidates.venue: ACM Transactions on Architecture and Code Optimization (TACO)

candidates.abstract: Subject indexing assigns descriptors from a controlled vocabulary to bibliographic records, a task characterized by thousands of labels, few positive examples per label, and a long tail of rarely used descriptors. Existing extreme multi-label classifiers treat the vocabulary as a flat list, ignoring the semantic relations that thesauri encode. We present TAGHN, a heterogeneous graph re-ranker over a per-document subgraph of retrieved candidates augmented with the thesaurus neighborhood. The relevance of a candidate descriptor is estimated jointly from its similarity with the document and also the degree to which the candidate’s thesaurus neighborhood matches the document content. A decomposed scoring head combines interpretable graph-derived features with retrieval signals. On STW, an economic thesaurus of 6,198 descriptors, TAGHN reaches 0.380 macro F1 against 0.346 for a fine-tuned cross-encoder and 0.278 for a fixed-vocabulary XMLC classifier. In terms of micro F1, it outperforms re-ranking models and stays competitive (-3.0) with the best fixed-vocabulary XMLC model. Qualitative analysis shows the graph resolving errors that per-label scoring cannot, selecting a narrower gold descriptor where an unstructured re-ranker settles for its broader parent.
candidates.title: Reading the neighborhood: Text-Attentive Graph Reranking for Automated Subject Indexing
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 26th ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries

candidates.abstract: With the widespread adoption of online social networks, social recommender systems have become a key paradigm for mitigating data sparsity and cold-start issues in traditional collaborative filtering. However, existing graph neural network (GNN) based recommendation models face two fundamental structural bottlenecks when dealing with real-world social data: social noise and over-smoothing. Invalid or weak social connections dilute preference signals, while representation homogenization induced by deep graph convolution undermines personalized recommendation. To address these challenges, this report proposes a new framework named SRIGB (Social Recommendation via Information Graph Bottleneck). SRIGB introduces the Information Bottleneck principle as a principled denoising mechanism by maximizing the mutual information between the denoised graph and interaction labels while minimizing redundant information with respect to the original noisy graph, thereby extracting task-relevant social structure more precisely. In addition, SRIGB incorporates a contrastive learning paradigm to counteract the smoothing effect of graph convolution, enabling the model to preserve high-order social influence while maintaining discriminative and independent user representations. This report presents the theoretical foundations, model architecture, and experimental design of SRIGB, aiming to provide both theoretical support and a practical technical pathway for building the next generation of robust social recommender systems.
candidates.title: Sparsity-aware social recommendation via information graph bottleneck

candidates.abstract: Entities in real-world systems often evolve over time: users shift between information consumption patterns, researchers migrate between fields, and firms transition between financial risk states. When such systems are modeled as dynamic graphs, these transitions correspond to nodes whose class labels change between consecutive snapshots, which we call shifters. Correctly classifying shifters is often more consequential than classifying stable nodes with persistent labels, as detecting such transitions enables timely intervention in high-stakes settings. Yet, we identify a systematic failure mode across all major dynamic graph neural network architectures: shifter performance consistently lags behind stable nodes, with errors concentrated on the old label. Our structural analysis traces this failure to embedding inertia: neighborhood aggregation keeps shifter representations anchored to the old-class centroid, and this effect is strongest precisely where it is hardest to correct, namely for shifters whose neighborhoods remain aligned with the old class. Guided by this finding, we propose CHASE, a model-agnostic CHange-Aware framework for Shifting nodEs that wraps any dynamic GNN with targeted components for detecting label shifts and overriding stale neighborhood signals. CHASE consistently improves shifter performance across all tested models and datasets (up to 114.9% and 202.5% improvement on accuracy and F1 score, respectively) while preserving stable-node performance. We additionally contribute three dynamic graph benchmarks with naturally shifting labels, filling a gap in existing resources. The source code is available at https://github.com/jhkim611/CHASE
candidates.title: Chasing Label Shifters: A Change-Aware Framework for Dynamic Graph Node Classification

candidates.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) commonly assume that node features are fully observed, despite missing features being pervasive in real-world applications. By leveraging the dependence between node features and graph structure, existing graph-specific methods handle missingness by propagating observed feature values along graph edges. However, these methods have mainly been evaluated in overly optimistic settings, where feature entries are removed independently and uniformly across the graph. This overlooks realistic scenarios in which missingness propagates among connected nodes, as can occur during localized sensing failures in sensor networks. We formalize this complementary notion as graph-structured mask dependence, where the joint distribution of missingness indicators is shaped by the graph, and introduce a controlled mechanism that instantiates this setting. We study propagation-based methods theoretically and empirically in this setting, showing that their effectiveness changes substantially compared with the uniformly random regime. Motivated by this limitation, we propose PEMix, designed to remain effective under challenging graph-structured missingness. Rather than propagating observed values, PEMix uses global structural representations to condition a probabilistic model of incomplete node features before message passing. Experiments under controlled graph-structured missingness and naturally occurring missingness show that PEMix remains robust across complex missingness regimes, with particularly strong performance as missingness becomes severe.
candidates.title: When Missingness Follows the Graph: Beyond Feature Propagation for Missing Features

candidates.abstract: Wildfire decisions are made in hours, yet most learned spread models predict daily on targets including burned area. We propose FireGraphNet which formulates 12-hour growth as node classification on directed H3 graphs, with candidates ahead of the front and wind alignment, terrain, fuel continuity and barriers on edges. On satellite perimeters it achieves average precision 1.7-1.9x the strongest distance baseline on test California fires and 1.62x out of state. We show this skill comes from message passing rather than cell features or the aggregator, is highest on young fires in state, is carried deep along the wind by its edges, and is hidden by pooling. A convolutional network matches this ranking once trained on new growth, at worse calibration, so candidate construction, target definition, and aggregation shape conclusions about model skill. Editing fuel and barrier attributes reduces predicted spread more under guided than random placement, extending FireGraphNet to operational intervention analysis.
candidates.title: FireGraphNet: Sub-daily wildfire spread prediction with directed graph neural networks
Predicting LogP values using multi-strategy Graph Neural Networks: a complementary approach to protein-based biomarker discovery in cancer research

candidates.abstract: Day-ahead (DA) electricity price forecasting is usually posed per market, with a separate model fitted to each grid's own history. This caps accuracy: statistical and tree-based baselines saturate, while higher-capacity sequence models need more training data than a single market's few years of hourly prices can supply. Such methods also treat each node as an independent series, discarding the spatial dependencies induced by network topology and congestion. Because price formation across independent system operators (ISOs) is driven by shared physics and largely common market design, we instead treat cross-market history as a pretraining corpus. We present MetaGrid, a topology-aware transformer, meta-trained across markets so that a single zone-count-independent parameter set adapts to an unseen grid. On a leak-free benchmark of five U.S. ISOs, where every model receives the same prices, DA load forecasts and calendar features, MetaGrid attains the lowest average MAE, improving on the best baseline by 3.1\% and on the same architecture trained from scratch by 7.7\%.
candidates.title: Cross-Market Meta-Learning for Electricity Price Forecasting

candidates.abstract: Adversarial detection on evolving attributed graphs faces two challenges: fraud labels arrive late or not at all, and natural distributional drift erodes any trained decision boundary. Modern detectors can reach strong detection rates when labels are available and the distribution is stationary; sustaining that quality without labels and under drift is the open problem. We identify feature-context consistency -- the alignment between a node's attributes and its aggregated neighborhood attributes -- as a single structural signal that addresses both. We formalize it as the Context Boost (CB) score within a Restricted Boltzmann Machine framework (CB-RBM) and prove two complementary worst-case guarantees: a strict separation between the expected CB of legitimate and adversarial nodes, with gap growing linearly in model capacity, whenever the adversary's context stays far enough from legitimate neighborhood context; and a Wasserstein-Lipschitz bound on how far the CB distribution moves under natural drift. We validate on XBlock Ethereum phishing (~153K nodes) and Reddit banned-user detection (~11K nodes), with two further datasets in the appendix spanning diverse domains. With zero labels, CB-RBM achieves AUROC>= 0.96 on four adversarial attacks and keeps FPR close to its calibrated 5% target under drift -- outperforming supervised GNNs (hundreds of labels), unsupervised graph-anomaly baselines, and a standard RBM whose FPR collapses to 89-100%. What typically requires separate mechanisms -- label-free operation and drift stability -- here follows from a single structural regularity of the data. Code: https://github.com/serval-uni-lu/CB-RBM.
candidates.title: Feature-Context Consistency: Unsupervised Adversarial Detection with Drift Stability on Attributed Graphs

candidates.abstract: Social media platforms generate vast volumes of user-generated content that often obscure meaningful discourse, a phenomenon conceptualized as social noise. While existing misinformation detection methods primarily focus on factual verification, they largely overlook the role of social noise in amplifying misinformation. This study assesses the performance of six text-based models and a graph neural network (GNN) in mitigating the effects of misinformation using predefined social noise constructs. The dataset consists of 500,000 tweets collected from the X platform using the Ukraine hashtag during the Russia-Ukraine conflict from March 2024 to March 2025. Advanced machine learning models achieve strong performance, with accuracies ranging from 79.94% to 97.17%. RoBERTa demonstrates the highest performance, with an accuracy of 97.17%, Cohen's kappa of 0.9660, MCC of 0.9660, and AUC of 0.9977. The GNN achieves an accuracy of 64.52% and an AUC of 0.899, demonstrating performance above random-chance classification by exploiting the relational structure between tweets. All text-based models achieve kappa values greater than 0.75, indicating substantial overall agreement. Explainable AI analysis using LIME reveals that 89.6% of predictive weight is attributed to contextual features rather than isolated keywords. The findings highlight that integrating social noise into AI pipelines enhances misinformation detection and supports more effective mitigation strategies in large-scale social media environments.
candidates.title: Assessing the Performance of AI Models in Misinformation Detection Using Predefined Social Noise Constructs

candidates.abstract: Online platforms often expose activity signals even when records of the underlying connections are incomplete or delayed. These activity responses may retain indirect evidence of connections that formed during the observation period but are absent from the recorded topology. Recovering such hidden structural changes can help keep network records aligned with evolving interactions and support downstream network analysis. However, the effects of a change propagate through the network and may overlap, making state changes difficult to associate with specific connections. We propose the Hierarchical Structural Context Ranker (HSCR), which combines visible network structure with node-state changes to infer connections that have formed but remain unrecorded. By jointly modeling the topological context of state responses and associations among potential connections, HSCR converts distributed activity changes into evidence for distinguishing potential connections without prespecified dynamical equations or parameters. Experiments on five temporal-network benchmarks and a real temporal Reddit network validate its effectiveness. Across observation spans and structural-record delays, true added connections achieve a 36%-50% reduction in mean true rank relative to the corresponding best baselines. This work provides a principled way to prioritize unrecorded additions for structural verification and record maintenance in online communities, information networks, and other networked systems.
candidates.title: Inferring Hidden Structural Changes from Node-State Responses under Partial Network Observations

candidates.abstract: Multimodal entity alignment (MMEA) is fundamental to integrating heterogeneous knowledge graphs (KGs), yet existing paradigms remain critically vulnerable to incomplete modalities and cross-graph structural asymmetries. This paper exposes a fundamental oversight in current MMEA research: treating feature missingness and topological discrepancies as isolated preprocessing or denoising challenges, which overlooks their destructive coupling during multimodal fusion. We systematically formulate and evaluate two newly identified failure modes: 1) Detail Missing (DM)-induced overvaluation, where the absence of local modality details causes models to overemphasize uninformative, blurred representations; and 2) Context Imbalance (CI)-induced suppression, where topological discrepancies across KGs allow dense structural contexts to overwhelm weaker but highly discriminative modal signals, triggering high-level semantic drift. To break this cycle of degradation, we introduce ALMEA, a generative and calibration framework that establishes a bidirectional feedback loop between low-level feature reconstruction and high-level latent space alignment. Specifically, Cross-Modality Imputation (CMI) synthesizes missing modality details to mitigate overvaluation, while Latent Semantic Calibration (LSC) aligns cross-graph joint embeddings to suppress topology-driven semantic drift. Under sparse supervision, we develop Controlled Iterative Selection (CIS) to adaptively acquire representative and diverse pseudo-labeled pairs, optimizing latent calibration under constrained budgets. Extensive evaluations on standard benchmarks demonstrate that ALMEA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. At a 20% supervision rate, ALMEA yields substantial absolute improvements of up to 5.20% in MRR and 6.40% in Hits@1, maintaining robust gains across higher supervision thresholds.
candidates.title: Silence and Noise: Resolving Suppression and Overvaluation in Multimodal Entity Alignment

candidates.abstract: The global semiconductor industry has become a strategic pillar of the digital economy and mainly supports the artificial intelligence technology, cloud computing, advanced manufacturing, and modern electronic devices. Forecasting international semiconductor trade flows is therefore essential for governments, researchers, and policymakers. In this paper, we propose TradeGraph, a hybrid Graph Neural Network (GNN) architecture that combines Graph Attention Networks (GAT), Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) and GraphSAGE through an adaptive gated fusion mechanism for bilateral trade flow prediction. This research used the BACI international trade database. First, we analyze the structural evolution of the global semiconductor trade network and identify its major trading communities. Then, we develop a hybrid GNN model that we compare with three baseline GNN architectures under a temporal train-validation-test split, to predict the semiconductor trade flow. Experimental results demonstrate that TradeGraph achieves the best predictive performance and exhibits lower variability across multiple independent runs. Our results reveal that the global semiconductor market is characterized by a limited number of major trade blocs and suggest an increasing importance of Asian economies in the global semiconductor trade network over the study period. These findings demonstrate the potential of hybrid Graph Neural Networks for analyzing and forecasting complex international trade networks.
candidates.title: TradeGraph: Learning Global Semiconductor Market Dynamics from International Trade Networks using Hybrid Graph Neural Networks
candidates.venue: International journal of advances in soft computing and its applications

candidates.abstract: The matching between wiring modes and feeder automation (FA) levels in 10 kV urban distribution networks lacks systematic methods, particularly neglecting communication infrastructure constraints. This paper proposes a two-stage matching model based on graph attention networks (GAT) that fuses electrical, topological, and information and communication technology (ICT) features. A 360-scenario dataset is constructed from IEEE 33/69-node test systems, covering four wiring modes (single-radial, multi-section radial, two-supply ring, three-supply ring) and three FA levels (FA-I/II/III). The first stage employs GAT for wiring mode identification, achieving 91.7% accuracy. The second stage recommends optimal FA configurations through feature fusion with embedded ICT feasibility hard constraints, attaining 83.3% Top-1 matching accuracy. Transfer validation on 72 operational feeders from three Nanjing districts yields 87.5% wiring mode accuracy and 79.2% Top-1 FA matching. Communication features contribute a 3.1 percentage-point gain to matching accuracy, and the constraint mechanism effectively prevents infeasible FA recommendations in low-coverage scenarios. Ablation studies confirm the superiority of the two-stage cascaded architecture over end-to-end alternatives.
candidates.title: Optimal Matching of Ring and Radial Wiring Modes with Three-Level Feeder Automation Configuration in 10 kV Urban Distribution Networks Based on Graph Attention Networks
candidates.venue: EAI Endorsed Transactions on Energy Web

candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Spatial multi‐omics (transcriptome, epigenome, proteome, metabolome, morphomics), provide near‐panoramic omics profiles across tissues. However, cross‐integration of structurally unpaired and underutilized morphomic datasets (e.g., Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)‐stained images), remains a bottleneck due to inherent differences in spot structures, feature dimensions, and cellular heterogeneities. Here, we present AgaeSMO, an adaptive graph auto‐encoder for versatile cross‐modality integration of both structurally paired and unpaired spatial multi‐omics data. AgaeSMO encodes each omics modality from a cell type‐aware KNN (k‐nearest neighbor) feature graph and a spatial adjacency graph, while leverages GATs (Graph Attention Networks) as the backbone to fuse modalities by learning joint representations through an attention‐weighted module. It specially fuses structurally unpaired modalities, which applies a morphological transformation strategy by designing a cross‐guidance alignment among modalities through graph cross‐attention learning. H&E images are treated as a standalone morphomic modality (rather than auxiliary features) is specially fused with other modalities through image patch embeddings to fully utilize cellular morphological heterogeneities. AgaeSMO is a powerful tool can effectively integrate diverse omics modalities with both paired and unpaired spot architectures. These unique capabilities enable precise spatial domain delineation, micro‐environmental heterogeneity detection, compatible across broad platforms, that outperforming pre‐existing tools. AgaeSMO offers a versatile, robust framework for integrative spatial multi‐omics analysis and facilitates multimodal, biologically interpretable mining.
candidates.title: Flexible Integration of Structurally Diverse Spatial Multi‐Omics With AgaeSMO

candidates.abstract: Cooperative driving at mixed-traffic unsignalized intersections is challenged by imperfect vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication, human-driven vehicle (HV) intentions that cannot be directly communicated, and the potential incompatibility of independently generated crossing decisions. This paper proposes State-Intent-Aware Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving under Imperfect V2X (SIGN-MAPPO) to address these challenges through three coordinated mechanisms. Each decision-eligible connected and automated vehicle (CAV) first reconstructs a receiver-specific traffic graph from its ego state and the peer-state records available to it, from which a shared graph-attention policy generates a raw Stop/Go intention augmented with predicted HV-intent features. CAV intentions are then exchanged through timestamped vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) messages, and a local conflict-aware arbitration layer converts each CAV's intention into a safe executable action despite potentially inconsistent peer information. In the principal Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) evaluation, SIGN-MAPPO achieves a 97.53% completion rate, a 0.10% collision rate, and a mean intersection traversal time of 35.28 s. Ablation studies further confirm the complementary contributions of HV-intent prediction and CAV-intent exchange to this performance. The trained policy also remains robust under the evaluated communication-delay and packet-loss ranges, and cross-scenario tests show complete traffic clearance across the tested settings, though safety margins narrow under compound unpredictable HV behavior.
candidates.title: SIGN-MAPPO: State-Intent-Aware Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving under Imperfect V2X

candidates.abstract: In practical engineering and scientific computing, a real physical system can be reduced to a boundary value problem, and the adequate boundary information to determine the interior spatial distribution and evolutionary state of the physical field can be solved with linear equations, alternatively, the the real physical problem can be treated with boundary problems with in adequate information problems in field of machine learning. This paper proposes a deep learning framework for the recovery of missing boundary information using an attention-guided graph neural network (GNN) surrogate. The framework extracts features from the physical information on the discretized boundary into a latent space, and the missing boundary quantities are then predicted by the network. Thus, the nonlinear mapping from known boundary quantities to missing boundary quantities is learned using a variational autoencoder (VAE) architecture, while an attention mechanism is incorporated to better model the correlations among different types of boundary information. Furthermore, the interior physical field can be reconstructed using the conventional boundary element method (BEM) integral formulation. The effectiveness of the GNN-BEM framework is evaluated using numerical examples of the two-dimensional Laplace and Poisson equations, which demonstrate good performance in reconstruction accuracy, local detail preservation, and model stability. The results show that GNN-BEM provides a feasible computational framework for boundary information recovery and fast interior physical field reconstruction for partial differential equations under complex boundary conditions.
candidates.title: An Attention-Guided Graph Neural Network Surrogate for Boundary Integral Computation in Physical Field Reconstruction

candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong potential for text-attributed graph learning by leveraging rich pre-trained knowledge and language understanding capabilities. Combining LLMs with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) offers a promising paradigm for expanding the modeling capabilities of graph learning. However, LLMs and GNNs follow distinct learning paradigms, leading to a pronounced mismatch between their knowledge spaces. Such discrepancies make effective knowledge fusion nontrivial. Moreover, existing methods often incur substantial additional computation for only limited performance gains. To address these challenges, we propose DeKoR, an efficient framework for GNN and LLM knowledge fusion. To enable efficient knowledge transfer, DeKoR decomposes LLM knowledge into complementary local and global views and uses the LLM as an offline teacher to distill them into lightweight experts. To enable selective knowledge fusion, an adaptive router learns how much each node should rely on each expert. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that DeKoR outperforms existing baselines on both node and subgraph classification, achieving superior effectiveness and efficiency.
candidates.title: DeKoR: Decomposed Knowledge Routing for Efficient GNN--LLM Fusion

candidates.abstract: To evaluate whether a compact bidirectional state-space autoencoder improves joint classification of species, cell type, and disease state from single-nucleus RNA-sequencing profiles in heart failure (HF), while yielding interpretable gene attributions. Building on the dense denoising autoencoder (DAE) and MLP framework of Ruz Jurado et al., we developed scHFBiMamba, combining a bidirectional Mamba autoencoder (BiMambaAE) with an MLP head. BiMambaAE maps 16,545-gene profiles to 350-dimensional latent representations using 13.2M parameters, about 14.6-fold fewer than the dense DAE (192.9M). We compared six encoder-classifier configurations on 38,275 held-out cardiac nuclei using McNemar tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and assessed nine classifiers on frozen representations. Biological relevance was evaluated by comparing SHAP-derived differentially explained genes with differentially expressed genes against curated HF-related Gene Ontology keywords. BiMambaAE+MLP achieved the highest aggregate F1: pooled macro-F1 across 13 outputs was 0.966 versus 0.957 for DAE+MLP, and the mean category macro-F1 was 0.977 versus 0.970. It significantly improved cell-type and disease-state accuracy (adjusted p=7.1e-3 and p=4.8e-6, respectively), with species F1 of 1.000. SHAP-derived differentially explained genes achieved a pathway-enrichment benchmark F1 of 0.105 versus 0.053 for differentially expressed genes. Compact bidirectional state-space autoencoders can outperform substantially larger dense autoencoders for joint cardiac transcriptomic classification while reducing parameters. scHFBiMamba enables accurate multi-task prediction and hypothesis-generating gene-level interpretation. Code: https://github.com/UgoLomoio/scHFBiMamba.
candidates.title: scHFBiMamba: a bidirectional Mamba autoencoder for cardiac disease-state classification from single-nucleus RNA-seq data
Spatio-temporal graph foundation models for earth system intelligence: an end-to-end, continual, and multimodal learning framework

candidates.abstract: Bus operations are inherently unstable---buses initially dispatched at equal headways will inevitably end up bunching up. This issue exacerbates passenger waiting times, creates load imbalances between buses, and undermines service reliability. Reinforcement learning (RL) has proven highly effective for mitigating bus bunching and outperforms traditional model-based approaches. However, existing RL approaches require agents to continuously interact with the environment, which potentially disrupts the bus system before effective policies are learned. This paper proposes an Offline Graph-based Multi-agent Actor-Critic (Offline-GMAC) method that trains bus holding policies using only readily available logged GPS data collected during normal uncontrolled operations, thereby eliminating the need for disruptive online interaction or exploration. The method employs general graph neural networks for multi-agent credit assignment. A key innovation of our method is a data augmentation scheme that synthesizes unperformed holding actions from historical uncontrolled bus trajectories. The scheme exploits the equivalence between stochastic link travel time delays and deliberate holding interventions. Under mild assumptions, we prove that the 1-Wasserstein distance between synthesized and target state transition distributions is bounded above by a term that scales linearly with the standard deviation of link travel times plus a tunable synthesis-dependent term. Evaluations using real-world bus data demonstrate that the proposed offline method achieves performance comparable to, and in some cases, even better than its online counterpart.
candidates.title: From Observation to Intervention: Mastering Bus Holding Control from Historical Uncontrolled Trajectories with Offline Reinforcement Learning

candidates.abstract: Multi-robot systems (MRS) offer significant advantages over single-robot platforms by enabling information sharing and coordination for different tasks in complex environments. However, reliable cooperation critically depends on inferring trust over both information sources and their reported hypotheses, particularly under partial observability and potential adversarial interference. Existing approaches frequently depend on pre-established trust relationships or side-channel information, which may not be available or reliable in realistic MRS deployments. This work introduces NeST-Bayes, a neural-symbolic framework that jointly infers robot and hypothesis trust using only inter-robot observation consistency, without requiring preassigned robot trust, reputation information, or side-channel identity signals. NeST-Bayes infers instantaneous trust evidence scores for robots and object hypotheses by reasoning over ego-centric relational graphs constructed from cross-robot observation consistency. These evidence scores are accumulated over time through Bayesian updates of Beta-distributed trust beliefs to maintain temporally consistent trust estimates. Extensive evaluations show that NeST-Bayes achieves the highest mean object precision and robot recall across all benchmark settings, and the highest robot precision and object recall in most settings, compared to trust-based methods. Under aggressive optimized attacks, it achieves 98.8\% robot precision with 93.8\% recall and 98.3\% object precision with 95.4\% recall. In an occlusion-rich Webots warehouse, it maintains 92.5\% robot precision with 92.0\% recall and 97.3\% object precision with 85.0\% recall. These results demonstrate joint improvements in the reliability and coverage of retained information.
candidates.title: Who to Trust in Multi-Robot Systems: Joint Robot and Object Hypothesis Trust Inference via Neural-Symbolic Cross-Validation

candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed molecular prediction and design, yet these advances remain only partially integrated with experimental discovery. We define TechBio 3.0 as an emerging paradigm for closed-loop drug discovery that connects multimodal molecular representations, generative chemistry, and automated experimentation. We examine its early preclinical and clinical evidence, identify remaining technical and translational barriers, and argue that this convergence is beginning to define biotechnology’s next era.
candidates.title: TechBio 3.0 closes the drug discovery loop with multimodal AI and generative chemistry

candidates.abstract: Learning how local perturbations affect a network is important for identifying which components drive or absorb a system's response. We formulate this as seed-conditioned response ranking: given a perturbation at one seed node, ranking all other nodes by response strength. This is challenging when the model is given only the interaction topology, while the mechanism governing how perturbations propagate must be learned from data. We present VQIL (Visible Quantum Interference Learning), a trainable Szegedy quantum walk for seed-conditioned ranking. Edge weights, link phases, and per-node phase rotations are optimized end-to-end by backpropagation while the walk operator remains unitary throughout training. Node scores are obtained from a geometrically discounted coherent sum of quantum-walk amplitudes, enabling quantum interference before the final squared-norm readout. Because each learned parameter is attached to a named edge or node, the trained model provides directly inspectable hypotheses about the roles of individual graph components in the propagation mechanism. On AC power-flow perturbations over six transmission grids, with electrical parameters withheld from the model, VQIL improves Spearman rank correlation from 0.147 for the untrained walk to 0.831 and outperforms an identically trained random-walk model. On gene perturbation over five protein-protein interaction networks with Perturb-seq supervision, VQIL improves rank correlation from 0.171 to 0.620, outperforming the strongest learned classical and neural baselines. These results show that trainable quantum-walk interference provides a scalable and interpretable inductive bias for learning seed-conditioned response rankings on graphs.
candidates.title: VQIL: Visible Quantum Interference Learning for Perturbation Response Ranking on Graphs

candidates.abstract: Skeleton-based action recognition has advanced significantly with graph convolutional networks that model joints as nodes and bones as edges. However, conventional graphs are inherently limited to pairwise connections and are less effective at representing group-wise coordination patterns in human motion, where multiple joints often act as a functional unit during complex movements such as swinging or throwing. Hypergraphs provide a natural alternative by allowing hyperedges to connect arbitrary numbers of joints and explicitly encode coordinated joint groups. We propose the Motion-Guided Channel-Wise Hypergraph Convolutional Network (MC-HGCN), which models skeleton sequences through a unified hypergraph structure with three complementary mechanisms. MC-HGCN first constructs anatomical body-part and cross-limb hyperedges to provide structural priors. A motion-guided modulation mechanism adaptively reweights the hypergraph incidence matrix according to per-frame joint motion intensity, dynamically emphasizing active joint groups. Furthermore, a channel-wise hyperedge learning module discovers distinct coordination patterns across feature channels, enabling feature-specific relational modeling. A residual pathway preserves fine-grained pairwise information to complement high-order hypergraph aggregation. Extensive experiments on NTU RGB+D 60 and NTU RGB+D 120 demonstrate that MC-HGCN achieves strong performance using only joint coordinates, with notable improvements on high-motion actions involving complex multi-joint coordination. Ablation studies and visualization analyses further validate the effectiveness of each proposed component.
candidates.title: Motion guided Channel wise Hypergraph convolutional network for skeleton action recognition
MalGraphNet: an adversarially robust heterogeneous graph neural network for behaviour-based malware classification using API semantics and control flow topology
candidates.venue: Journal of Computer Virology and Hacking Techniques

candidates.abstract: Accurate assessment of urban patrol cases plays an important role in maintaining urban safety and improving the efficiency of urban governance. The hazard level of urban patrol cases can be reflected by the urgency level and prioritizing high-urgency cases can help reduce potential risks to public safety. However, it remains challenging to assess the urgency level of urban patrol cases when reliable urgency labels are limited or unavailable. To address this problem, this paper proposes an urban patrol case urgency classification method based on self-supervised clustering of a graph neural network. First, a case-relationship graph is constructed from urban patrol cases. A graph attention-based autoencoder is then pretrained to learn node representations, and K-means is used to initialize cluster centers. Finally, representation learning and clustering are jointly optimized to identify urgency-oriented clusters without using manual labels during training. Experimental validation was conducted using 6126 urban patrol case records from Zhengzhou, China. The proposed method achieved a Recall of 0.7458, Precision of 0.7465, ACC of 0.7424, F1 of 0.7403, and NMI of 0.4517. Compared with TADW, the strongest baseline, the proposed method improved these metrics by 0.0617, 0.0479, 0.0650, 0.0690, and 0.0407, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively learn urgency-related latent representations and improve the classification quality of urban patrol cases.
candidates.title: An urban patrol case urgency classification method based on self-supervised clustering of a graph neural network

candidates.abstract: The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based maritime surveillance is becoming an important part of maritime Internet of Things (IoT) and intelligent transportation systems. It provides a flexible and cost-effective way to large-scale maritime traffic monitoring. However, achieving robust situational awareness remains challenging in practical maritime environments. The main challenges arise from heterogeneous sensing modalities, adverse imaging conditions, and spatial misalignment caused by UAV motion. To address these problems, this paper proposes an airborne multi-modal graph learning-driven framework, termed AMGT, for vessel identification and tracking in UAV-assisted maritime IoT. Specifically, visible and infrared images are first aligned and fused through a multi-parameter perspective transformation model. This improves visual perception under low visibility and complex illumination conditions. Automatic identification system (AIS) messages are then temporally synchronized using interpolation and linear prediction. To detect small and oriented vessels, we develop a mixed-modality MAir-YOLOv8-OBB detector, followed by the MAir-SORT algorithm for stable vessel tracking. We further design a graph learning-driven association network to model temporal dynamics and spatial dependencies among vessels and between vessels and UAVs. A motion-aware coordinate unification (MCU) strategy is also introduced to reduce nonlinear misalignment caused by UAV motion. Experiments on the MAP-M2UAV50 dataset show that AMGT achieves high accuracy and efficiency. The results demonstrate its potential for UAV-assisted maritime IoT applications, including vessel monitoring, traffic situational awareness, and intelligent maritime transportation services. The dataset and code will be available at https://github.com/MAPGroup/AMGT.
candidates.title: Multi-Modal Graph Neural Network-Inspired Vessel Identification and Tracking for UAV-Based Maritime Surveillance

candidates.abstract: In navigating the challenges of computational and communication overhead within the 6G-era Collaborative Inference (CI), this paper explores the feasibility of employing Stacked Intelligent Metasurface (SIM) to perform CI, termed SIM-CI. The SIM functions as a physical computing unit, receiving multi-user Over-The-Air (OTA) aggregated features within the same spectrum. It thus executes the necessary spatial-frequency combining and inference in a single physical wave propagation.SIM-CI also incorporates a tri-heterogeneity robustness adapter to address the network heterogeneity, such as multi-modal data and user inference models, as well as a quality-aware contrastive approach that align features from different modalities and extraction levels into a unified feature space. Considering the heterogeneous and dynamic channels, we further integrate Channel State Information (CSI) as an additional input into the adapter design, enabling users'early perception of potential channel states. Moreover, to maximally mitigate the impact of channel variations, we design a new hybrid beamforming network that combines the robustness of model-driven pre-equalization with the adaptability of data-driven learning. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our SIM-CI compared to digital-domain inference, achieving 98.6\% accuracy to conversional digital-domain CI approaches under various heterogeneous conditions, while reducing computational energy by 25\% and requiring 75\% fewer transmission time slots.
candidates.title: Stacked Intelligent Metasurface-Based MultiModal Feature Fusion for Collaborative Inference in Edge Networks

candidates.abstract: Hypergraph Neural Networks (HNNs), designed to model higher-order relations beyond pairwise interactions, typically rely either on fixed structural weights or on normalised attention. Fixed weights can propagate misleading information in heterophilic settings, while normalisation makes attention coefficients competitive, in the sense that, in a message-passing framework, increasing the weight of one sender must reduce the weight of others in the same aggregation set. Our main contribution is the introduction of PANDA (Prior-guided AttentioNal Dual-path Architecture), a plug-in for two-stage message passing HNNs applicable to both undirected and directed settings. The main path interpolates between learned receiver-normalised attention and structural incidence priors, while a non-competitive (not normalised) auxiliary path lets each sender contribute its own transformed information. We also show that, with fixed structural coefficients, PANDA recovers a certain complex-valued convolution operator adopted in previous works. Across four HNNs spanning spatial and spectral methods in both directed and undirected settings, plugging PANDA in yields an average improvement of 5.18 percentage points across eight real-world benchmark datasets. The code is available at https://github.com/jainris/panda.
candidates.title: PANDA: Prior-guided Attentional Dual-path Architecture

candidates.abstract: Anticipation of vessel trajectories is an essential task when navigating at sea. This applies to both human navigators and autonomous surface vessels. Trajectory forecasting enables sub-routines such as collision avoidance to assess the situation and react accordingly in time. This paper investigates Transformer and Performer models for trajectory prediction of surface vessels in confined waters. Using widely available position data from the Automatic Identification System (AIS), candidate models are trained and evaluated. Historical information on how other vessels have moved in the local area surrounding each agent is conveyed using positional heat maps.
